About 35 centimetres long, it had two dorsal fins, long leaf-shaped paired fins and broad tooth plates for crushing shellfish and other hard-shelled prey. Like modern lungfish it could probably gulp air when the water became warm and stale.
entries.v: 最早的肺鱼之一，来自约3.85亿年前苏格兰奥卡迪亚盆地的中泥盆世湖泊。它体长约35厘米，有两个背鳍、长长的叶状偶鳍，以及用于压碎贝类和其他硬壳猎物的宽大齿板。和现代肺鱼一样，当水变得温暖而缺氧时，它很可能会吞咽空气。

entries.k: One of the earliest mammaliaforms, a shrew-like animal about 10 centimetres long that lived from the latest Triassic into the Early Jurassic. Its sharp teeth suggest it hunted insects, and thousands of its teeth and bones have been recovered from ancient cave and fissure fillings in south Wales. Its lower jaw still had the old reptilian joint working alongside the new mammal-type joint, a step in the evolution of the mammalian middle ear.
entries.v: 最早的哺乳形类之一，一种形似鼩鼱、体长约10厘米的动物，生活在三叠纪末至早侏罗世。锋利的牙齿表明它捕食昆虫，人们已从威尔士南部的古代洞穴和裂隙堆积中找到了数千颗它的牙齿和骨骼。它的下颌仍保留着旧的爬行类关节，与新的哺乳类关节并行工作，这是哺乳动物中耳演化中的一步。

entries.k: One of the earliest scorpions, about 4 cm long, from the Late Silurian Bertie Group of New York, about 420 million years ago. It already had the scorpion body plan: grasping pincers, four pairs of walking legs and a curled tail ending in a sting. It lacks clear evidence of book lungs, so it probably still lived in shallow water or at its edges rather than fully on land.
entries.v: 最早的蝎子之一，体长约4厘米，来自纽约州晚志留世的伯蒂群，距今约4.2亿年。它已具备蝎子的身体构型：可抓握的螯、四对步足和末端带毒刺的卷曲尾部。目前没有它具有书肺的明确证据，因此它可能仍生活在浅水中或水边，而不是完全登上陆地。

entries.k: One of the earliest trilobites, from the early and middle Cambrian of China and Australia: a spiny, crescent-headed scavenger and predator. Redlichia rex from South Australia grew to about 12 cm and had spiny legs for tearing up its food.
entries.v: 最早的三叶虫之一，出自中国和澳大利亚的早、中寒武世：一种多刺、头部呈新月形的食腐者和捕食者。南澳大利亚的霸王莱德利基虫体长约12厘米，用带刺的足撕碎食物。

entries.k: One of the earliest true ankylosaurs, about 3-4 metres long, from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Wyoming. Its low, broad body was covered from neck to tail in rows of conical bony osteoderms, with longer spikes along its flanks and a heavily armoured skull. It had no tail club, so it relied almost entirely on its armour, crouching low so predators could not reach its soft belly.
entries.v: 最早的真正甲龙类之一，体长约3-4米，生活在美国怀俄明州晚侏罗世的莫里森组。它低矮宽阔的身体从颈部到尾部覆盖着成排的锥形骨质鳞甲，体侧长着更长的尖刺，头骨也有厚重的装甲。它没有尾锤，因此几乎完全依靠装甲防御，伏低身体让掠食者够不着柔软的腹部。

entries.k: One of the earliest true starfish, from the Late Ordovician (Katian) of the Cincinnati region, a few centimetres across. Its small disc and five short, broad arms were built of neat rows of block-like plates, with large plates along the edges of each arm. Early starfish like it crept over the sea floor on tube feet and probably fed on small animals and organic debris.
entries.v: 最早的真海星之一，发现于辛辛那提地区的晚奥陶世（凯迪期）地层，直径只有几厘米。它小小的体盘和五条短而宽的腕由排列整齐的块状骨板构成，每条腕的边缘都有大型骨板。像它这样的早期海星靠管足在海底爬行，可能以小动物和有机碎屑为食。

entries.k: One of the earliest vascular land plants: leafless, branching stems a few centimetres tall, tipped with spore capsules.
entries.v: 最早的陆生维管植物之一：无叶、分叉的茎高仅数厘米，顶端生有孢子囊。

entries.k: One of the earliest vertebrates, a small jawless fish about 6 cm long from the Burgess Shale and the nearby Marble Canyon site of British Columbia. It had a pair of large camera eyes, zig-zag muscle blocks along its body and seven pairs of gill bars. The first pair of bars was a little thicker than the rest, foreshadowing the gill arch that later became jaws. Specimens from Marble Canyon were described in 2014.
entries.v: 最早的脊椎动物之一，一种体长约6厘米的小型无颌鱼，来自伯吉斯页岩及附近不列颠哥伦比亚省的大理石峡谷化石点。它有一对大型相机眼、沿身体排列的"之"字形肌节和七对鳃弓。第一对鳃弓比其余稍粗，预示了后来演化成颌的鳃弓。大理石峡谷的标本于2014年被描述。

entries.k: One of the earliest vertebrates, from the Chengjiang biota, Yunnan.
entries.v: 最早的脊椎动物之一，来自云南澄江生物群。

entries.k: One of the earliest well-known ray-finned fishes, the group that now includes almost all living fish, from the Middle Devonian lakes of northern Scotland about 385 million years ago. Usually 25 to 55 centimetres long, it had large eyes, long toothed jaws and tiny diamond-shaped scales. It could swallow prey up to a third of its own length, including other fishes.
entries.v: 已知最早的辐鳍鱼之一——这一类群如今几乎囊括了所有现生鱼类——来自约3.85亿年前苏格兰北部的中泥盆世湖泊。它通常长25至55厘米，有大眼睛、长着牙齿的长颌和细小的菱形鳞片。它能吞下长达自身体长三分之一的猎物，包括其他鱼类。

entries.k: One of the earliest well-known sharks, from the Late Devonian Cleveland Shale of Ohio, about 370 million years ago, reaching up to about 1.8 metres. It had a streamlined body with a crescent-shaped tail, big triangular pectoral fins, spined dorsal fins and a mouth at the very front of the snout. Its skin was almost free of scales, and fossil stomach contents show it swallowed fishes and shrimp tail-first after chasing them down.
entries.v: 最早为人熟知的鲨鱼之一，出自俄亥俄州晚泥盆世的克利夫兰页岩，距今约3.7亿年，体长可达约1.8米。它身体呈流线型，尾鳍呈新月形，胸鳍大而呈三角形，背鳍带棘，口位于吻部最前端。它的皮肤几乎没有鳞片，胃内容物化石显示它追上鱼和虾后从尾部开始整个吞下。

entries.k: One of the earliest whales, from the early Eocene of Pakistan about 50 million years ago. It was a wolf-sized land mammal with slender legs, small hooves and a long tail that waded in shallow streams, but its ear bones already had the thick, shell-like form of a whale's. Its eyes sat on top of its long head, like a crocodile's.
entries.v: 最早的鲸类之一，生活在约5000万年前巴基斯坦的早始新世。它是一种体型与狼相仿的陆生哺乳动物，四肢纤细，长着小蹄和长尾，会在浅溪中涉水，但它的耳骨已具有鲸类那种厚实的贝壳状结构。它的眼睛像鳄鱼一样长在长长的头部顶端。

entries.k: One of the early goniatites, ammonoids from the Middle Devonian seas of New York, Europe and North Africa, about 390 million years ago. Its smooth, flattened shell, about 10 to 15 centimetres across, was loosely coiled with a wide central hollow and carried fine, strongly curved growth lines. Ammonoids first appeared in the Devonian, and like their later relatives they used gas-filled chambers to float while hunting small prey.
entries.v: 早期棱菊石之一，属于约3.9亿年前生活在美国纽约州、欧洲和北非中泥盆世海洋中的菊石类。它光滑扁平的壳直径约10到15厘米，松散地盘卷，中央有宽阔的脐凹，表面带有细密而强烈弯曲的生长线。菊石类最早出现于泥盆纪，和它们后来的亲属一样，它们利用充气的气室漂浮，同时捕食小型猎物。

entries.k: One of the first animals to build a hard skeleton: a lumpy crust up to a metre across that filled cracks in the reefs of what is now Namibia about 548 million years ago. Its body was a maze of thin mineral walls and channels, probably a sponge or a coral-like animal straining food from the water. Huge, rooted and almost all skeleton, it can soak up enormous damage, but it cannot move or strike back.
entries.v: 最早构建坚硬骨骼的动物之一：一块直径可达一米的瘤状硬壳，约 5.48 亿年前填满了今纳米比亚一带礁体的裂隙。它的身体是由薄薄的矿质隔壁和通道组成的迷宫，可能是一种从水中滤食的海绵或类珊瑚动物。它巨大、固着，几乎全是骨骼，能承受极大的伤害，但既不能移动也无法反击。

entries.k: One of the first four-limbed vertebrates, known from Late Devonian rocks of East Greenland about 365 million years old. It had a broad flat skull, heavy overlapping ribs that braced its chest, seven toes on each paddle-like hind foot and a fish-like tail fin. It probably lived mostly in shallow water and heaved itself across mudflats on its stout forelimbs, more like a seal than a walking lizard.
entries.v: 最早的四肢脊椎动物之一，发现于东格陵兰约3.65亿年前的晚泥盆世岩层。它有宽扁的头骨、支撑胸腔的粗重叠置肋骨、每只桨状后足上的七个趾，以及鱼一般的尾鳍。它可能大部分时间生活在浅水中，用粗壮的前肢拖着身体爬过泥滩，更像海豹而不是行走的蜥蜴。

entries.k: One of the first reptiles to return to the water, about 1 metre long, from the Early Permian of Brazil, Uruguay and southern Africa, around 280 million years ago. It swam with its long, deep tail and webbed hind feet, and its long, narrow jaws bristled with long, needle-like teeth for catching or straining small crustaceans. It lived in a vast, shallow, salty inland sea. Finding the same small coastal reptile, which could not have crossed an ocean, in both South America and Africa was early evidence that the two continents were once joined.
entries.v: 最早重返水中的爬行动物之一，体长约1米，生活在约2.8亿年前早二叠世的巴西、乌拉圭和非洲南部。它用又长又高的尾巴和有蹼的后足游泳，细长的颌部密布细长的针状牙齿，用来捕捉或滤食小型甲壳类。它生活在一片广阔、浅而咸的内陆海中。这种无法横渡大洋的小型沿岸爬行动物同时出现在南美洲和非洲，成为两块大陆曾经相连的早期证据。

entries.k: One of the first reptiles, found inside fossil tree stumps at Joggins, Nova Scotia.
entries.v: 最早的爬行动物之一，发现于新斯科舍省乔金斯的树桩化石内。

entries.k: One of the giant sea scorpions, about 1.6 m long, from the Late Silurian and Early Devonian of Britain. In front of its small head shield it carried a pair of enormous, toothed pincers that could reach far forward, and its big compound eyes gave it sharp vision. Paddle-like hind legs and a broad, flat tail fin made it an active hunter that seized fish and other sea scorpions, the most powerful predator of its seas.
entries.v: 巨型海蝎之一，体长约1.6米，生活于英国的晚志留世和早泥盆世。它小小的头甲前方长着一对巨大的、带齿的螯肢，可以远远地向前伸出，一对大复眼让它视力敏锐。桨状的后足和宽而扁平的尾鳍使它成为主动出击的猎手，能捕捉鱼类和其他海蝎，是当时海洋中最强大的掠食者。

entries.k: One of the heaviest bony fish, over two tonnes, shaped like a swimming head with tall fins and no real tail. It eats mostly jellyfish, basks on its side at the surface to warm up, and a female can carry 300 million eggs.
entries.v: 最重的硬骨鱼之一，体重超过两吨，外形像一颗游动的大头，长着高耸的鳍，却没有真正的尾巴。它主要以水母为食，会侧躺在水面晒太阳取暖，一条雌鱼可怀卵3亿枚。

entries.k: One of the heaviest flying birds, weighing up to 15 kg with a wingspan that can exceed three metres. Groups fish together, swimming in a horseshoe to drive fish into the shallows and scooping them up in the stretchy throat pouch. It nests in large colonies on lakes and deltas from south-eastern Europe to Africa and Asia, and soars on thermals between feeding grounds.
entries.v: 最重的飞行鸟类之一，体重可达15千克，翼展可超过三米。它们成群协作捕鱼，排成马蹄形游动，将鱼赶到浅水处，再用富有弹性的喉囊舀起。它在从东南欧到非洲和亚洲的湖泊与三角洲上集群筑巢，借助热气流在觅食地之间翱翔。

entries.k: One of the largest "bear-dogs", from the Middle Miocene of North America, weighing perhaps 500 kg. Amphicyonids were carnivorans with a bear-like body, a wolf-like head and a long, heavy tail. Its strong forelimbs suggest it grappled with large prey such as horses and camels.
entries.v: 最大的“犬熊”之一，出自北美中中新世，体重可能达500千克。犬熊类是食肉目动物，有熊一样的身体、狼一样的头和又长又重的尾巴。它强壮的前肢表明它会与马和骆驼等大型猎物搏斗。

entries.k: One of the largest African gorgonopsians, about 3 metres long, from the Late Permian of South Africa around 255 million years ago. Its skull was extraordinarily broad and heavy, with flaring cheek bones, rough bony bosses and huge sabre-like upper canines driven by powerful jaw muscles. It delivered some of the most devastating bites of its time and could tackle large dicynodonts and pareiasaurs. Its bulk made it strong but not especially quick.
entries.v: 非洲最大的丽齿兽类之一，体长约 3 米，生活在约 2.55 亿年前二叠纪晚期的南非。它的头骨异常宽阔沉重，颧骨向外扩展，长有粗糙的骨质瘤突，强壮的颌肌驱动着巨大的军刀状上犬齿。它的咬击是当时最具毁灭性的之一，能够对付大型二齿兽和锯齿龙。庞大的身躯让它力大无穷，但并不特别敏捷。

entries.k: One of the largest Early Jurassic ichthyosaurs, up to about 9 metres long, from the seas of England and Germany around 195 million years ago. Its eyes were about 25 cm across, among the largest of any animal ever, letting it hunt in dim, deep water. A fast, dolphin-shaped swimmer with a long toothed snout, it was the top predator of its seas and even fed on other ichthyosaurs, though its slim body had little protection.
entries.v: 早侏罗世最大的鱼龙之一，体长可达约9米，约1.95亿年前生活在英格兰和德国的海洋中。它的眼睛直径约25厘米，是有史以来所有动物中最大的眼睛之一，使它能在昏暗的深水中捕猎。它是游速很快、形似海豚的游泳者，长着带齿的长吻，是当时海洋中的顶级掠食者，甚至会捕食其他鱼龙，不过它纤细的身体几乎没有防护。

entries.k: One of the largest Silurian trilobites, up to about 18 cm long, from the Rochester Shale of New York. Its very broad, flat shell was covered in tubercles, with a large swollen glabella, thorax segments drawn out into flat spines and a big tail shield fringed with broad spines. Slow-moving and heavily armoured, it fed on organic debris on the sea floor and was a hard, spiny mouthful for any predator.
entries.v: 志留纪最大的三叶虫之一，体长可达约18厘米，发现于美国纽约州的罗切斯特页岩。它非常宽阔扁平的外壳布满瘤突，有一个巨大隆起的头鞍，胸节延伸成扁平的刺，宽大的尾甲边缘排列着宽刺。它行动缓慢、装甲厚重，以海底的有机碎屑为食，对任何掠食者来说都是又硬又扎嘴的一口。

entries.k: One of the largest amphibians that ever lived, up to about 5 metres long, from the Middle Triassic lakes and deltas of southern Germany, about 240 million years ago. Its huge, flat, triangular skull was over a metre long, with eyes on top and two big tusks in the lower jaw whose tips poked up through holes in the snout. With its small limbs and flattened body it lived in the water like a giant salamander, ambushing fish and other animals.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的两栖动物之一，体长可达约5米，来自德国南部中三叠世的湖泊和三角洲，距今约2.4亿年。它巨大、扁平的三角形头骨长逾1米，眼睛长在头顶，下颌有两颗大獠牙，其尖端从吻部的孔中向上穿出。它四肢短小、身体扁平，像巨型蝾螈一样生活在水中，伏击鱼类和其他动物。

entries.k: One of the largest animals ever to walk the Earth, a titanosaur about 37 metres long and some 55-60 tonnes from Patagonia about 100 million years ago. It is known from the bones of at least six individuals, so its size is better established than that of most giant sauropods. Fully grown, it was simply too big for any predator to bring down, and its sheer bulk was its defence.
entries.v: 有史以来在地球上行走的最大动物之一，一种体长约37米、重约55至60吨的泰坦巨龙，约1亿年前生活在巴塔哥尼亚。它至少有六个个体的骨骼被发现，因此它的体型比大多数巨型蜥脚类更确切。完全长成后，它体型大到任何掠食者都无法将其撂倒，庞大的身躯就是它的防御。

entries.k: One of the largest animals of its time, a radiodont about half a metre long from the Burgess Shale of Canada, whose head was covered by an enormous flattened shell. It swam low over the seabed, raking the mud with comb-like front limbs for small animals. Its sheer bulk and huge armoured head make it extremely hard to bring down, but it is a slow, clumsy swimmer and not a strong fighter.
entries.v: 当时最大的动物之一，是一种体长约半米的放射齿目动物，来自加拿大的伯吉斯页岩，头部覆盖着一块巨大而扁平的甲壳。它贴着海底游动，用梳子般的前肢耙梳泥土寻找小动物。它庞大的身躯和巨大的装甲头部让它极难被击倒，但它游得缓慢笨拙，也不善战斗。

entries.k: One of the largest animals of the Late Devonian seas, about 370 million years ago: an armoured placoderm that may have reached 5 to 7 metres long. Despite its size and heavy head-and-shoulder armour, its long jaws were small-mouthed and toothless, and it probably cruised slowly through open water filtering out small prey, much like a basking shark. Its sheer bulk made it very hard for any predator to bring down.
entries.v: 晚泥盆世海洋中最大的动物之一，生活在约3.7亿年前：一种披甲的盾皮鱼，体长可能达5至7米。尽管体型庞大、头肩部覆有厚重甲板，它细长的颌部口小而无齿，很可能像姥鲨一样在开阔水域中缓慢巡游，滤食小型猎物。凭借庞大的体型，任何掠食者都很难将它击倒。

entries.k: One of the largest carnivorous land mammals, a bear of Pleistocene North America that stood about 1.6 m at the shoulder on all fours and weighed up to 900 kg. Its long legs and short face once suggested a fast hunter, but studies of its bones point to a varied diet, with much scavenging of large carcasses. It died out about 11,000 years ago.
entries.v: 体型最大的陆生食肉哺乳动物之一，是北美更新世的一种熊，四足站立时肩高约1.6米，体重可达900千克。它的长腿和短脸曾让人认为它是快速的猎手，但对其骨骼的研究表明它食性多样，很大程度上以大型动物尸体为食。它约在1.1万年前灭绝。

entries.k: One of the largest dicynodonts of the Late Permian, about 2 metres long, from South Africa around 256 million years ago. It had a very broad, heavy skull with a toothless horny beak, a pair of tusks and big, rough bosses on the snout, possibly used in shoving contests between rivals. Its massive, barrel-shaped body gave it great staying power, letting it absorb punishment that would kill smaller plant-eaters.
entries.v: 二叠纪晚期最大的二齿兽之一，体长约 2 米，生活在约 2.56 亿年前的南非。它的头骨非常宽阔沉重，长有无齿的角质喙、一对獠牙以及吻部巨大粗糙的瘤突，可能用于对手之间的推挤较量。它粗壮的桶状身体赋予它极强的耐力，能承受足以杀死较小植食动物的伤害。

entries.k: One of the largest duck-billed dinosaurs, around 9-12 metres long, from western North America about 73-68 million years ago. It had a long, low head with a broad toothless beak and no bony crest, but a mummified specimen shows a fleshy comb on top of its head. Huge bonebeds suggest it lived in large herds, and some skeletons carry healed Tyrannosaurus bite marks.
entries.v: 最大的鸭嘴龙类之一，体长约9至12米，生活在约7300万至6800万年前的北美西部。它的头长而低，有宽阔无齿的喙，没有骨质头冠，但一件木乃伊化标本显示它头顶有一个肉质的冠。大型骨层表明它们结成大群生活，有些骨骼上带有已愈合的霸王龙咬痕。

entries.k: One of the largest flying animals ever, with a wingspan of about 10-11 metres and the standing height of a giraffe. It probably launched itself by vaulting on its folded wings and stalked small animals on foot like a giant stork. Late Cretaceous of North America.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的飞行动物之一，翼展约10-11米，站立时与长颈鹿一样高。它可能靠折叠的翅膀撑地跃起起飞，并像巨型鹳一样徒步追踪小动物。生活于北美洲晚白垩世。

entries.k: One of the largest flying birds known, from the Late Miocene of Argentina, with a wingspan of about 6-7 m and a weight of some 70 kg. A teratorn, related to New World vultures, it was too heavy to flap for long and must have soared on the strong westerly winds and thermals off the Andes. Its large, hooked bill suggests it swallowed small prey whole as well as scavenging.
entries.v: 已知最大的飞鸟之一，生活在阿根廷的晚中新世，翼展约6至7米，体重约70千克。它属于畸鸟类，是新大陆秃鹫的近亲，体重太大，无法长时间扇动翅膀，只能借助强劲的西风和安第斯山脉的上升热气流翱翔。它巨大的钩状喙表明，它除了食腐，还会把小型猎物整个吞下。

entries.k: One of the largest flying fish, up to about 40 cm long, feeding on plankton near the surface of warm seas. To escape tuna and dolphinfish it bursts out of the water, sculls along the surface with the long lower lobe of its tail, then glides on its wing-like pectoral and pelvic fins for 100 metres or more. Juveniles carry a pair of fringed chin barbels, which give the species its name.
entries.v: 最大的飞鱼之一，体长可达约40厘米，在温暖海域的表层以浮游生物为食。为躲避金枪鱼和鲯鳅，它会冲出水面，用尾鳍延长的下叶在水面划动，然后展开翼状的胸鳍和腹鳍滑翔100米甚至更远。幼鱼长有一对带流苏的颏须，该物种因此得名。

entries.k: One of the largest flying insects ever, with a wingspan of about 70 centimetres. This griffinfly, a relative of modern dragonflies, hunted other insects over the swampy coal forests of the Late Carboniferous, about 300 million years ago. Its size was possible partly because the air then held much more oxygen than today. It is known from fossils found at Commentry, France.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的飞行昆虫之一，翼展约70厘米。这种巨脉蜻蜓是现代蜻蜓的亲戚，约3亿年前在晚石炭世沼泽般的煤炭森林上空捕食其他昆虫。它能长这么大，部分原因是当时空气中的氧气远比今天丰富。它因法国科芒特里发现的化石而为人所知。

entries.k: One of the largest land mammals ever, standing about 4 m at the shoulder, from the Middle and Late Miocene of Europe. Unlike elephants it had no upper tusks; instead a pair of thick lower tusks curved down and back from the tip of its lower jaw, probably used to strip bark and pull down branches. Its long legs suggest it walked long distances through open woodland. Deinotheres were a side branch of the proboscideans that died out in the Early Pleistocene.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的陆生哺乳动物之一，肩高约4米，来自欧洲的中新世中期和晚期。与大象不同，它没有上獠牙；取而代之的是一对粗壮的下獠牙，从下颌前端向下、向后弯曲，可能用来剥树皮和拉下树枝。它的长腿表明它能在开阔林地中长途跋涉。恐象类是长鼻类的一个旁支，在早更新世灭绝。

entries.k: One of the largest land predators ever, about 12 metres long and 8 tonnes, with the strongest bite of any known land animal, strong enough to crush bone. It lived in western North America at the very end of the Cretaceous, until the asteroid impact 66 million years ago.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的陆地掠食者之一，体长约12米，体重8吨，咬合力是已知陆地动物中最强的，足以咬碎骨头。它生活在白垩纪末期的北美洲西部，直到6600万年前的小行星撞击。

entries.k: One of the largest land predators of the Early and Middle Triassic, about 245 million years ago in southern Africa, reaching about 5 metres long. Its enormous head made up about a fifth of its length, with long jaws full of big curved teeth, on a bulky body with sturdy half-sprawling legs. One of the first giant archosaur relatives after the end-Permian extinction, it could overpower large plant-eating synapsids, but it was slow and heavy.
entries.v: 早三叠世至中三叠世最大的陆地掠食者之一，约2.45亿年前生活在非洲南部，体长约5米。它巨大的头部约占体长的五分之一，长长的颌部布满弯曲的大牙，身体粗壮，四肢结实、半直立。作为二叠纪末大灭绝后最早出现的巨型主龙类近亲之一，它能制服大型植食性合弓类，但行动缓慢而笨重。

entries.k: One of the largest land predators of the Late Jurassic, a heavily built megalosaurid about 9-10 metres long from western North America. Its long, deep skull held long, serrated, blade-like teeth, and its short arms were unusually powerful, with big thumb claws. It could tackle sauropods and stegosaurs, but its bulk made it slower than lighter hunters.
entries.v: 晚侏罗世最大的陆地掠食者之一，是一种体格粗壮的斑龙类，体长约9-10米，生活在北美洲西部。它又长又深的头骨里长着细长、带锯齿的刀状牙齿，短小的前肢却异常强壮，长有巨大的拇指爪。它能对付蜥脚类和剑龙，但庞大的身躯使它比体型较轻的猎手更慢。

entries.k: One of the largest land-dwelling amphibians of its time, about 2 metres long, from the earliest Permian of Texas and New Mexico. Its huge, broad, flat head, about a quarter of its length, held many sharp teeth and fangs on the palate. It had a sturdy skeleton and strong legs and probably lived much like a crocodile, catching fish and smaller tetrapods in swamps and rivers. It belongs to the temnospondyls, a large group of early amphibians.
entries.v: 同时代最大的陆生两栖动物之一，长约2米，来自美国得克萨斯州和新墨西哥州的最早二叠世地层。它巨大、宽阔而扁平的头部约占体长的四分之一，长着许多锋利的牙齿，上颚还有獠牙。它骨骼粗壮、四肢强健，生活方式可能很像鳄鱼，在沼泽和河流中捕食鱼类和较小的四足动物。它属于离片椎类，一个庞大的早期两栖动物类群。

entries.k: One of the largest palaeodictyopterans, beaked insects of the coal forests, known from the Mazon Creek beds of Illinois, about 309 million years old. Its wings spanned perhaps 50 to 55 centimetres, rivalling the griffinflies, and like other palaeodictyopterans it could not fold them back over its body. It had a pair of small winglets in front of the wings and a long piercing-sucking beak, probably used to drink sap or suck out the spores and seeds of plants.
entries.v: 最大的古网翅类之一，古网翅类是煤炭森林中长着喙的昆虫。它发现于伊利诺伊州的梅森溪地层，距今约3.09亿年。它的翼展大约有50至55厘米，可与巨脉蜻蜓相媲美；和其他古网翅类一样，它无法把翅膀向后折叠到身体上。它在翅膀前方有一对小翅片，还有一根长长的刺吸式喙，可能用来吸食植物汁液，或吸出植物的孢子和种子。

entries.k: One of the largest phytosaurs, up to about 7 metres long, from the Late Triassic rivers of Arizona about 225 million years ago. It looked much like a giant crocodile, with a long, deep snout full of teeth and thick bony armour on its back, but its nostrils sat on a mound just in front of the eyes instead of at the tip of the snout. It lay in wait in the water and seized fish and animals that came to drink.
entries.v: 最大的植龙类之一，体长可达约7米，生活在约2.25亿年前晚三叠世的亚利桑那河流中。它看上去很像一条巨鳄，长而高的吻部布满牙齿，背上覆有厚重的骨甲，但它的鼻孔长在眼前的一个隆起上，而不是吻端。它潜伏在水中，捕捉鱼类和前来饮水的动物。

entries.k: One of the largest predators of the Early Jurassic, about 7 metres long, from the Kayenta Formation of Arizona, around 190 million years old. It is named for the pair of thin, half-moon crests along the top of its skull, probably used for display. A notch behind the narrow snout tip gave its upper jaw a kinked profile. The frill and venom of the Jurassic Park film are fiction; its real skull was strong and its teeth suited to large prey.
entries.v: 早侏罗世最大的掠食者之一，体长约7米，来自亚利桑那州的卡岩塔组，距今约1.9亿年。它因头骨顶部一对薄薄的半月形头冠而得名，这对头冠可能用于展示。狭窄的吻端后方有一个缺口，使其上颌呈弯折状轮廓。电影《侏罗纪公园》中的颈部褶伞和毒液纯属虚构；它真实的头骨很结实，牙齿适合捕食大型猎物。

entries.k: One of the largest predatory dinosaurs of the Triassic, about 5 metres long, from Germany about 210 million years ago. It was a lightly built, long-legged relative of Coelophysis, with a long neck, grasping three-fingered hands and possibly a pair of thin crests along its snout. Fast and agile, it could hunt the young of the big plant-eater Plateosaurus, but its slim frame could not take much punishment.
entries.v: 三叠纪最大的肉食性恐龙之一，体长约5米，约2.1亿年前生活在德国。它是腔骨龙的近亲，体格轻盈、腿长，脖子很长，三指的手能抓握，吻部上方可能有一对薄薄的冠。它敏捷迅速，能捕猎大型植食恐龙板龙的幼体，但纤细的身体经不起重创。

entries.k: One of the largest terror birds of the Oligocene of Patagonia, a flightless predator about 2 m tall. It was heavier and slower than its lanky later relatives, but its huge, deep, hooked beak could split open prey with downward hatchet blows. Its beak strike was among the hardest blows of any Paleogene hunter, but it had little to protect itself in a drawn-out fight.
entries.v: 渐新世巴塔哥尼亚最大的恐鹤之一，是一种身高约2米、不会飞的掠食者。它比后来身材修长的亲戚更重、更慢，但巨大而高耸的钩状喙能像斧头一样向下劈开猎物。它的喙击是古近纪猎手中最猛烈的打击之一，但在持久的战斗中它几乎没有什么自我保护。

entries.k: One of the largest trilobites ever, up to about 60 centimetres long, from the Middle Devonian seas of New York and Ontario, about 390 million years ago. It bristled from head to tail with spines and knobs: long spines on its cheeks, along every body segment and around its tail shield. This spiky armour made it a near-impossible mouthful even for the big armoured fish of its time, though it was slow and had little to fight back with.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的三叶虫之一，体长可达约60厘米，来自约3.9亿年前纽约州和安大略省的中泥盆世海洋。它从头到尾布满棘刺和瘤突：颊部有长刺，每个体节和尾甲周围也都长着刺。这身多刺的铠甲让它即使对当时的大型披甲鱼类来说也几乎无法下咽，不过它行动缓慢，几乎没有还击能力。

entries.k: One of the largest trilobites that ever lived, from the Middle Ordovician of Portugal, Spain and Bohemia: complete shields over 40 cm long are known, and some may have reached 60 cm or more. Its broad, flat, oval body had short cheek spines and a big, wide tail shield. It lived in cool, muddy seas on the edge of the southern supercontinent Gondwana, and its sheer size made it very hard for predators to kill.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的三叶虫之一，生活在葡萄牙、西班牙和波希米亚的奥陶纪中期：已知完整的背甲长逾40厘米，有些个体可能达到60厘米甚至更长。它宽阔扁平的椭圆形身体上长着短短的颊刺和宽大的尾甲。它生活在南方超大陆冈瓦纳边缘寒冷而多泥的海洋中，庞大的体形使捕食者极难将它杀死。

entries.k: One of the last and largest dicynodonts, a hippo-like plant-eater about 3.5 metres long and weighing up to a tonne, from the Late Triassic of Arizona about 220 million years ago. It cropped plants with a toothless horny beak and had a pair of short tusks growing from bony bosses on its upper jaw. The remains of about 40 individuals were found together in the Placerias Quarry near St. Johns, Arizona, suggesting it lived in herds.
entries.v: 最后也是最大的二齿兽类之一，是一种形似河马的植食动物，体长约3.5米，体重可达1吨，生活在约2.2亿年前亚利桑那州的晚三叠世。它用无齿的角质喙啃食植物，上颌的骨质隆突上长着一对短獠牙。在亚利桑那州圣约翰斯附近的扁肯氏兽采石场中发现了约40个个体的遗骸聚集在一起，表明它们可能群居生活。

entries.k: One of the most abundant dolphins, living in fast-moving schools of hundreds or even thousands in warm and temperate seas worldwide. It is recognised by the criss-cross 'hourglass' on its flanks, tan-yellow in front and grey behind. Schools work together to herd fish and squid into tight balls, finding them by echolocation.
entries.v: 数量最多的海豚之一，以数百甚至数千头的快速游动群体生活在全球温暖和温带海域。它体侧有交叉的“沙漏”花纹，前部黄褐色、后部灰色，易于辨认。群体借助回声定位找到鱼类和鱿鱼，并协作将它们驱赶成紧密的球团。

entries.k: One of the most common trilobites of the Late Ordovician seas around Cincinnati, Ohio, typically 3-5 cm long. Its strongly arched shell had a bell-shaped, lobed glabella, small eyes and a thorax of thirteen segments, with no spines. It is very often found rolled up into a tight ball, a defence that protected its soft underside from predators and from smothering mud.
entries.v: 晚奥陶世俄亥俄州辛辛那提一带海洋中最常见的三叶虫之一，体长通常为3-5厘米。它高高拱起的外壳上有钟形分叶的头鞍、小眼睛和由十三节组成的胸部，没有棘刺。它常常被发现蜷成紧密的球状，这种防御方式能保护柔软的腹面免受掠食者伤害和淤泥窒息。

entries.k: One of the oldest and largest penguins, from the late Paleocene of New Zealand, about 1.6 m long and perhaps 100 kg. It shows that penguins became flightless, wing-propelled divers and giants within a few million years of the end-Cretaceous extinction. It had a long, narrow beak for catching fish and squid.
entries.v: 最古老、最大的企鹅之一，出自新西兰晚古新世，体长约1.6米，体重可能达100千克。它表明，在白垩纪末大灭绝后的短短几百万年内，企鹅就已演化成不会飞、靠翅膀推进的潜水者和巨型种类。它有长而窄的喙，用来捕捉鱼和乌贼。

entries.k: One of the oldest armoured fish, a jawless vertebrate from the Late Ordovician coastal seas of Colorado, about 455 million years ago. Its head was encased in a shield of many small bony plates carved with fine ridges, and inside lay one of the oldest known cartilage braincases. Slow and toothless, it fed on small particles near the bottom, trusting its heavy armour to protect it.
entries.v: 最古老的披甲鱼类之一，是一种无颌脊椎动物，生活在约4.55亿年前美国科罗拉多州奥陶纪晚期的近岸海域。它的头部包裹在由许多刻有细脊的小骨片组成的盾甲中，里面是已知最古老的软骨脑颅之一。它游得慢，也没有牙齿，在海底附近滤食细小颗粒，全靠厚重的盔甲保护自己。

entries.k: One of the oldest coral-like cnidarians with a hard skeleton, found in Cambrian rocks of western New South Wales, Australia, and North Greenland, about 510 million years old. Its colonies were clusters of cup-shaped corallites that budded from one another. Each cup had internal septa and was closed by a lid whose inner face also bore septa, something no living coral has. Its relationship to later corals is still debated.
entries.v: 已知最古老的具硬质骨骼的类珊瑚刺胞动物之一，发现于澳大利亚新南威尔士州西部和格陵兰北部约 5.1 亿年前的寒武纪地层中。它的群体由一簇彼此出芽生成的杯状珊瑚单体组成。每个杯体内部有隔板，杯口由一块盖子封闭，盖子内侧同样长有隔板——这是现生珊瑚所没有的特征。它与后来珊瑚的亲缘关系至今仍有争议。

entries.k: One of the oldest insects known, from the hot-spring wetlands of Rhynie in Scotland, about 410 million years ago. Only its tiny head has been found, but its strong, triangular, toothed jaws are like those of winged insects, hinting that insects may have taken to the air far earlier than their oldest known wings. Tiny and fragile but breeding in huge numbers, it would have swarmed among the first low land plants.
entries.v: 已知最古老的昆虫之一，来自约4.1亿年前苏格兰莱尼的温泉湿地。人们只发现了它微小的头部，但它强壮的三角形带齿颚与有翅昆虫的颚相似，暗示昆虫飞上天空的时间可能远早于已知最古老的翅膀化石。它微小而脆弱，却能大量繁殖，很可能成群地生活在最早的低矮陆生植物之间。

entries.k: One of the oldest known centipedes, from the Middle Devonian of Gilboa, New York, about 386 million years ago, and around a centimetre long. It already had a pair of venom claws under its head, long antennae and a flat body with a pair of legs on each segment. It hunted small arthropods in the leaf litter of some of the earliest forests, and is the only member of its own extinct order, Devonobiomorpha.
entries.v: 已知最古老的蜈蚣之一，来自纽约州吉尔博阿的中泥盆世，距今约3.86亿年，体长约1厘米。它头下已有一对毒爪，触角很长，身体扁平，每个体节有一对足。它在地球上最早的一批森林的落叶层中捕食小型节肢动物，是其自身所属的已灭绝目——泥盆蜈蚣目的唯一成员。

entries.k: One of the oldest known griffinflies, with a wingspan of about 32 centimetres, from the Late Carboniferous of Hagen-Vorhalle in Germany, about 320 million years ago. Like its giant relative Meganeura it had huge eyes, a strong thorax, four long veined wings and spiny legs that formed a basket for snatching prey in mid-air. A fast, agile aerial hunter of other flying insects, it struck hard but had a fragile body.
entries.v: 已知最古老的巨脉蜻蜓之一，翼展约32厘米，生活在约3.2亿年前德国哈根-福尔哈勒的晚石炭世。和它的巨型亲戚巨脉蜻蜓一样，它有巨大的眼睛、强壮的胸部、四片布满翅脉的长翅膀，以及组成“篮子”在空中抓捕猎物的多刺的腿。它是捕食其他飞虫的迅捷灵活的空中猎手，出击凶猛，但身体脆弱。

entries.k: One of the oldest known pterosaurs, from the Late Triassic of northern Italy about 210 million years ago, with a wingspan of about one metre. Its short jaws held more than a hundred tiny teeth, many of them with three to five cusps, and fish scales found in a fossil's gut show that it caught fish. Like other early pterosaurs it had a long, stiffened tail.
entries.v: 已知最古老的翼龙之一，出自意大利北部约2.1亿年前的晚三叠世，翼展约一米。它短短的颌中有一百多颗细小的牙齿，其中许多带有三到五个齿尖；化石胃中发现的鱼鳞表明它会捕鱼。与其他早期翼龙一样，它有一条僵直的长尾。

entries.k: One of the oldest known radiolarians, from the middle Cambrian of Australia: a drifting single cell with a spherical lattice shell of glass (silica) bristling with long radial spines. Along the spines it spread threads of cytoplasm to catch smaller plankton. Radiolarian skeletons, sinking for half a billion years, have built up thick layers of siliceous ooze and chert on the ocean floor.
entries.v: 已知最古老的放射虫之一，发现于澳大利亚的寒武纪中期地层：它是一个漂浮的单细胞，有着玻璃质（二氧化硅）的球形格子状外壳，上面密布着长长的放射状骨针。它沿着骨针伸展出细胞质丝，捕捉更小的浮游生物。五亿年来，放射虫的骨骼不断沉降，在洋底堆积出厚厚的硅质软泥层和燧石层。

entries.k: One of the oldest known scorpions, about 2.5 cm long, from the Early Silurian of Wisconsin, about 437 million years ago. It already had grasping pincers, large eyes and a curled tail ending in a sting, and its heart and blood vessels were arranged much like those of living scorpions. It probably hunted small animals in shallow water and at the shoreline. Tiny and fragile, it packed a dangerous sting for its size.
entries.v: 已知最古老的蝎子之一，体长约2.5厘米，生活于约4.37亿年前美国威斯康星州的早志留世。它已经具备抓握的螯、大眼睛和末端带毒刺的卷曲尾部，心脏和血管的排列与现生蝎子十分相似。它可能在浅水和岸边捕食小动物。虽然身体细小脆弱，但就体型而言它的毒刺十分危险。

entries.k: One of the oldest known synapsids, the group that much later produced mammals, found in fossilised tree stumps at Florence, Nova Scotia, about 306 million years old. It looked like a lizard about half a metre long, but its skull already had the single opening behind each eye typical of synapsids. Its sharp teeth, including enlarged ones near the front of the upper jaw, suggest it hunted insects and small tetrapods in the coal forests.
entries.v: 已知最古老的合弓类之一——这一类群在很久以后演化出了哺乳动物——发现于加拿大新斯科舍省弗洛伦斯的化石树桩中，距今约3.06亿年。它看起来像一只约半米长的蜥蜴，但头骨上每只眼睛后方已经具有合弓类典型的单个颞孔。它锋利的牙齿，包括上颌前部的几颗增大的牙齿，表明它在煤炭森林中捕食昆虫和小型四足动物。

entries.k: One of the oldest known vertebrates with a bony armour, from the Early to Middle Ordovician Stairway Sandstone of central Australia. About 15 cm long, it had flattened dorsal and ventral head shields joined by rows of small plates over the gills, tiny eyes at the front of the head, no paired fins and no jaws. Its body was covered in long, narrow, saw-edged scales, which gave it its name.
entries.v: 已知最古老的具骨甲脊椎动物之一，发现于澳大利亚中部早至中奥陶世的斯泰尔韦砂岩。它长约15厘米，扁平的背、腹头甲由鳃部上方的成排小骨板连接，头部前端有一对小眼，没有成对的鳍，也没有颌。它的身体覆盖着狭长、边缘呈锯齿状的鳞片，其名字便由此而来。

entries.k: One of the oldest known vertebrates, about 518 million years old, from the Chengjiang biota of Yunnan, China. Only about 3 cm long and without jaws, it had a sail-like dorsal fin, a fin fold along the belly, zig-zag blocks of muscle along its body and five or six gill pouches behind the head.
entries.v: 已知最古老的脊椎动物之一，距今约5.18亿年，出自中国云南澄江生物群。它仅约3厘米长，没有颌，长有帆状背鳍、沿腹部的鳍褶、沿身体排列的之字形肌节，以及头后的五六个鳃囊。

entries.k: One of the oldest known vertebrates, from the Chengjiang fauna: a skull and paired eyes around the chordate nerve cord.
entries.v: 已知最古老的脊椎动物之一，来自澄江动物群：脊索动物的神经索前端有头骨和成对的眼睛。

entries.k: One of the oldest pterosaurs, with a wingspan of about 1.2 metres, from the Late Triassic of the Austrian Alps about 210 million years ago. It had a long, stiff tail, jaws with large front fangs and many small multi-cusped teeth behind, and a thin bony crest along the top of its snout. A quick, agile flier, it probably snatched fish and other small prey.
entries.v: 最古老的翼龙之一，翼展约1.2米，约2.1亿年前生活在晚三叠世的奥地利阿尔卑斯地区。它有一条长而僵硬的尾巴，颌前部长着大獠牙，后面是许多多尖的小牙，吻部顶端还有一道薄薄的骨冠。它飞行敏捷迅速，大概以鱼类和其他小型猎物为食。

entries.k: One of the oldest turtles from North America, a small freshwater turtle from the Early Jurassic of Arizona, about 190 million years ago. Its low, smooth shell had lost the spikes of earlier turtles, and it lived in streams and pools, feeding on small animals and plants. Safe inside its shell from most attackers, it was slow on land and had a weak bite.
entries.v: 北美洲最古老的龟类之一，是一种小型淡水龟，约1.9亿年前生活在美国亚利桑那州的早侏罗世。它低平光滑的背甲已经没有早期龟类的尖刺，栖息在溪流和水塘中，以小动物和植物为食。躲在壳里时大多数攻击者都奈何不了它，但它在陆地上行动缓慢，咬合力也很弱。

entries.k: One of the oldest turtles with a complete shell, about 1 metre long, from the Late Triassic of Germany about 210 million years ago. Its high, domed shell was edged with spiky plates, but it could not pull its head inside, so its neck was protected by bony spines, and its tail ended in a spiked club. It had a toothless beak, yet small teeth still grew on the roof of its mouth, a leftover from its ancestors.
entries.v: 最早拥有完整龟壳的龟类之一，体长约1米，来自约2.1亿年前德国的晚三叠世。它高高隆起的龟壳边缘镶着尖刺状骨板，但它无法把头缩进壳里，所以颈部由骨质棘刺保护，尾巴末端还有一个带刺的棒槌。它长着无牙的喙，但口腔顶部仍长有小牙齿，这是从祖先那里遗留下来的特征。

entries.k: One of the oldest undisputed corals, from early Cambrian (Botoman) reef rocks of the Moorowie Formation in the Flinders Ranges, South Australia. Its colonies were made of tightly packed, many-sided tubes (corallites) sharing their walls, with internal floors (tabulae) and short spines, and grew in mushroom- or pagoda-like shapes among archaeocyath sponges and microbial reef. It was first compared with tabulate corals, but whether it is related to them is still debated.
entries.v: 最古老的确证珊瑚之一，产自南澳大利亚弗林德斯山脉穆罗维组的早寒武世（波托米期）礁岩中。它的群体由紧密排列、彼此共用壁的多边形管状珊瑚个体组成，内有横板和短刺，在古杯类海绵和微生物礁之间长成蘑菇状或宝塔状。它最初被比作床板珊瑚，但两者是否有亲缘关系至今仍有争议。

entries.k: One of the oldest well-preserved bats, from the early Eocene lake beds of Wyoming's Green River Formation, about 14 cm long with a 37 cm wingspan. It already flew and probably echolocated like living insect-eating bats, but kept a claw on its index finger and a long tail. Moth scales have been found in its stomach.
entries.v: 保存完好的最古老蝙蝠之一，来自怀俄明州绿河组的早始新世湖相地层，体长约14厘米，翼展37厘米。它已经能飞行，可能也像现生食虫蝙蝠一样使用回声定位，但食指上还保留着爪，并有一条长尾。人们在它的胃里发现过蛾的鳞片。

entries.k: One of the world's most damaging plant pests, a half-millimetre mite recorded on more than a thousand kinds of plants. It pierces leaf cells and sucks out their contents, leaving pale speckles, and its colonies cover leaves in fine silk webbing. In warm weather a generation takes only about a week, so populations explode and quickly evolve resistance to pesticides.
entries.v: 世界上危害最大的植物害虫之一，一种半毫米长的螨，已在一千多种植物上有记录。它刺破叶片细胞吸食其内容物，留下浅色斑点，其群体会用细密的丝网覆盖叶片。在温暖天气里，一代只需约一周，因此种群数量爆发式增长，并迅速演化出对杀虫剂的抗性。

entries.k: Opabinia had five eyes and a grasping proboscis.
entries.v: 欧巴宾海蝎有五只眼和一根能抓握的长吻。

entries.k: Opisthokonts swim with a single flagellum at the back: the branch of the fungi, choanoflagellates and animals.
entries.v: 后鞭毛生物靠身后的单根鞭毛游动：这是真菌、领鞭毛虫和动物所在的分支。

entries.k: Otters hunt fish underwater in family groups.
entries.v: 水獭以家庭为单位在水下捕鱼。

entries.k: Our closest extinct relatives, who lived in Europe and western Asia from about 400,000 to 40,000 years ago. They were stocky and strong, with a large brain, a long low skull and a heavy brow, and were skilled hunters of large animals who made stone tools, controlled fire and buried their dead. Most people living today outside Africa carry a little Neanderthal DNA.
entries.v: 我们最近的已灭绝亲戚，约40万至4万年前生活在欧洲和西亚。他们身材敦实、强壮，脑容量大，头骨长而低平，眉骨粗重；他们是捕猎大型动物的能手，会制作石器、控制用火并埋葬死者。如今生活在非洲以外的大多数人都携带少量尼安德特人的DNA。

entries.k: Outgoing warm blood heats returning cold blood in flippers and legs.
entries.v: 在鳍肢和腿中，流出的温血加热回流的冷血。

entries.k: Oxygen diffuses in through a thin body wall.
entries.v: 氧气透过薄薄的体壁扩散进入。

entries.k: Paired tubules in each segment filter the body fluid (worms).
entries.v: 每个体节中成对的小管过滤体液（蠕虫）。
古新世–始新世极热事件

entries.k: Paleocene–Eocene Thermal Maximum (~56 Ma): rapid warming of ~5–8 °C
entries.v: 古新世–始新世极热事件（约 56 Ma）：迅速升温约 5–8 °C

entries.k: Pangaea assembling as Euramerica and Gondwana collide
entries.v: 欧美大陆与冈瓦纳碰撞，盘古大陆正在形成

entries.k: Pangaea begins to rift; strong 'megamonsoon' seasons
entries.v: 盘古大陆开始裂解；强烈的“超级季风”季节

entries.k: Pangaea fully assembled, with vast arid interiors
entries.v: 盘古大陆完全形成，内陆广阔干旱

entries.k: Pangaea is complete. Its interior dries out, mammal ancestors (synapsids) dominate the land, and the period ends with the largest mass extinction in Earth's history.
entries.v: 盘古大陆最终形成。其内陆变得干旱，哺乳动物的祖先（合弓类）主宰陆地，本纪以地球历史上最大的灭绝事件告终。

entries.k: Pangaea splits apart and warm, humid conditions spread. Dinosaurs dominate the land, giant sauropods roam, and the first birds take flight.
entries.v: 盘古大陆分裂，温暖湿润的气候扩散。恐龙主宰陆地，巨型蜥脚类四处漫游，最早的鸟类展翅飞翔。

entries.k: Pangaea splits into Laurasia and Gondwana; the Atlantic begins to open
entries.v: 盘古大陆分裂为劳亚大陆和冈瓦纳；大西洋开始张开

entries.k: Pangaea: one supercontinent in the Panthalassa ocean
entries.v: 盘古大陆：泛大洋中的唯一超大陆

entries.k: Parasites too big to swallow are walled off inside a capsule of cells.
entries.v: 大到无法吞噬的寄生虫被细胞囊包围隔离。
父母与幼崽生活在一起。
来自西伯利亚克麦罗沃的鹦鹉喙角龙类。

entries.k: Parrots: long-lived, clever, crack nuts with a strong beak.
entries.v: 鹦鹉：长寿、聪明，用强壮的喙破开坚果。
鹈鹕合作捕鱼，驱赶鱼群。

entries.k: Perhaps the spiniest of all trilobites, from the Middle Ordovician of the St Petersburg region of Russia. Its small, flat body was ringed with long, slender spines growing from its cheeks, every body segment and its tail, and a pair of very long spines rose from the back of its head and swept back over its body. The spines made it a painful mouthful for any predator, but it was a slow crawler with little bite of its own.
entries.v: 也许是所有三叶虫中刺最多的一种，生活在俄罗斯圣彼得堡地区的奥陶纪中期。它小而扁平的身体四周环绕着细长的刺，从颊部、每一个体节和尾部长出，头部后方还竖起一对极长的刺，向后弯过整个身体。这些刺让任何捕食者都难以下咽，但它爬行缓慢，自身几乎没有攻击力。

entries.k: Perhaps the strangest-looking ammonite, from the Late Cretaceous seas around Japan about 90 million years ago. After a few loose spiral whorls, its shell doubled back on itself in a chain of U-bends that wrap into a knot. The pattern looks random but follows a precise growth rule that kept the animal balanced, so it could drift through the water feeding on plankton.
entries.v: 或许是外形最奇特的菊石，出自约9000万年前日本周边的晚白垩世海洋。在几圈松散的螺旋之后，它的壳以一连串U形弯折回绕，缠成一团结。这种图案看似杂乱，实则遵循精确的生长规律，使动物保持平衡，从而能在水中漂流滤食浮游生物。

entries.k: Periods of stillness that save energy.

entries.v: 二叠纪–三叠纪大灭绝；极端高温

entries.k: Pigment cells that can change colour.
entries.v: 能改变颜色的色素细胞。

entries.k: Pit vipers sense heat and inject venom.
entries.v: 蝮蛇能感知热量并注射毒液。

entries.k: Placental mammals nourish the embryo through a placenta.
entries.v: 有胎盘类通过胎盘为胚胎提供营养。

entries.k: Planktonic foraminifera drift in the open sea with spiny, balloon-chambered shells.
entries.v: 浮游有孔虫漂浮在开阔的海洋中，外壳带有棘刺，房室呈气球状膨大。

entries.k: Polynesia, Micronesia and Fiji: volcanic islands and atolls of the Pacific.
entries.v: 波利尼西亚、密克罗尼西亚和斐济：太平洋的火山岛和环礁。

entries.k: Pressing together to keep warm (penguins, mice).
entries.v: 挤在一起保暖（企鹅、老鼠）。

entries.k: Primates: grasping hands, good eyes, big brains.
entries.v: 灵长类：能抓握的手、敏锐的眼睛、发达的大脑。

entries.k: Proteins that stop ice crystals forming in the blood.
entries.v: 阻止血液中形成冰晶的蛋白质。

entries.k: Pterosaurs flew on wings of skin; Quetzalcoatlus was as big as a giraffe.
entries.v: 翼龙用皮膜翅膀飞行；风神翼龙和长颈鹿一样大。

entries.k: Pulling back into a tube or shell when touched.
entries.v: 被触碰时缩回管中或壳里。

entries.k: Pushing into the middle of the group so others are on the outside.
entries.v: 挤到群体中央，让别的个体留在外围。

entries.k: Pushing, nipping or chasing a rival away from food or space.
entries.v: 推挤、轻咬或驱赶对手，使其远离食物或空间。

entries.k: REM sleep that consolidates memories (mammals, birds).
entries.v: 巩固记忆的快速眼动睡眠（哺乳动物、鸟类）。

entries.k: Raising body temperature to slow down pathogens.
entries.v: 升高体温以抑制病原体。

entries.k: Ratfish relative with a spiral whorl of teeth.
entries.v: 银鲛的亲戚，长着螺旋状齿轮。

entries.k: Ray-finned fish took over the open sea.
entries.v: 辐鳍鱼占领了开阔海洋。

entries.k: Rays flattened out; mantas filter plankton.
entries.v: 鳐类身体变得扁平；蝠鲼滤食浮游生物。

entries.k: Receptors that recognise molecules common to many microbes.
entries.v: 识别多种微生物共有分子的受体。

entries.k: Reef fish grazing sponges and algae.
entries.v: 啃食海绵和藻类的礁鱼。

entries.k: Reef fish specialised on coral polyps.

entries.v: 重新长出失去的身体部位。

entries.k: Releasing eggs and sperm into the sea.
entries.v: 把卵和精子释放到海中。

entries.k: Reptile with a neck longer than its body, from Monte San Giorgio, Switzerland.
entries.v: 脖子比身体还长的爬行动物，来自瑞士圣乔治山。

entries.k: Resting high off the ground, out of reach of predators.
entries.v: 在远离地面、掠食者够不到的高处休息。

entries.k: Resting in crevices or burrows out of sight.
entries.v: 在隐蔽的缝隙或洞穴中休息。

entries.k: Resting upside down, ready to drop into flight (bats).
entries.v: 倒挂休息，随时可落下起飞（蝙蝠）。

entries.k: Returning to the place of birth to breed (salmon, turtles).
entries.v: 返回出生地繁殖（鲑鱼、海龟）。

entries.k: Rhino-sized wombat relative, the largest marsupial ever.
entries.v: 犀牛大小的袋熊近亲，有史以来最大的有袋类。
随森林扩张而上升（估计 17–21%）

entries.k: Rising at night and sinking by day (plankton).
entries.v: 夜间上浮、白天下沉（浮游生物）。

entries.k: Rival males compete after mating, inside the female.
entries.v: 竞争的雄性在交配后于雌性体内继续竞争。

entries.k: Robbing other animals of their catch (skuas).
entries.v: 抢夺其他动物的猎获物（贼鸥）。

entries.k: Rolling in dust to remove excess oil and parasites.
entries.v: 在尘土中打滚，去除多余油脂和寄生虫。

entries.k: Rotaliids build chalky shells of many chambers coiled in a spiral, some with algae inside.
entries.v: 轮虫目有孔虫建造由许多房室螺旋盘绕而成的白垩质外壳，有些壳内还共生着藻类。

entries.k: Rubbing against rocks and trees to scrape off parasites.
entries.v: 在岩石和树干上蹭，刮掉寄生虫。

entries.k: Rubbing ants into the feathers for their formic acid.
entries.v: 把蚂蚁揉进羽毛，利用其蚁酸。

entries.k: Rubbing body parts together to chirp.
entries.v: 摩擦身体部位发出鸣声。

entries.k: Rubbing off the old skin, sometimes in one piece (snakes, lizards).
entries.v: 蹭掉旧皮，有时完整一张（蛇、蜥蜴）。
追跑猎物直至其力竭（人类）。

entries.k: Sabre-toothed gorgonopsian predator of the Karoo Basin, South Africa.
entries.v: 南非卡鲁盆地的剑齿丽齿兽类掠食者。

entries.k: Sail-backed semi-aquatic predator of North African rivers.
entries.v: 北非河流中背上有帆的半水生掠食者。

entries.k: Sail-backed synapsid, top predator of the Texas red beds.
entries.v: 背上有帆的合弓类，得克萨斯红层的顶级掠食者。

entries.k: Glands that make venom, delivered by fangs, stings or grooved teeth (scorpions, centipedes, snakes).
entries.v: 腺体分泌毒液，通过螯牙、螫针或带槽的牙齿注入（蝎子、蜈蚣、蛇）。

entries.k: Scandinavia, the Baltic and western Russia, which drifted from cold southern seas to the tropics.
entries.v: 斯堪的纳维亚、波罗的海地区和俄罗斯西部，从寒冷的南方海域漂移到热带。

entries.k: Scorpions came ashore and breathe with book lungs.
entries.v: 蝎子登上陆地，用书肺呼吸。

entries.k: Scratching itchy skin with a hind foot.
Scrolled nose bones that warm and moisten the air (warm-blooded animals).
entries.v: 卷曲的鼻甲骨，为空气加温加湿（温血动物）。

entries.k: Sea cows are the elephants' closest relatives.
entries.v: 海牛是大象最近的亲戚。

entries.k: Sea scorpions grew to 2.5 m long.
entries.v: 海蝎可长到 2.5 m 长。

entries.k: Sealed cells stocked with food for the larvae (wasps).
entries.v: 储满食物供幼虫食用的封闭巢室（胡蜂）。

entries.k: Searching the sea floor for food.
Sense the faint electric fields of hidden prey.
entries.v: 感知隐藏猎物发出的微弱电场。

entries.k: Senses water movement along the flanks.
Serpentine early whale from Wadi Al-Hitan, Egypt.
entries.v: 来自埃及鲸鱼谷的蛇形早期鲸类。

entries.k: Sessile animals fight for space by overgrowing or stinging their neighbours (corals).
entries.v: 固着动物通过覆盖生长或刺伤邻居来争夺空间（珊瑚）。

entries.k: Shaggy rhino of the Ice Age steppe.
entries.v: 冰期草原上毛发蓬松的犀牛。

entries.k: Shallow seas flood the continents (e.g. the Western Interior Seaway)
entries.v: 浅海淹没大陆（如西部内陆海道）

entries.k: Sharks keep replacing their teeth all their lives; megalodon was the largest.
entries.v: 鲨鱼终生不断换牙；巨齿鲨是其中最大的。
尖锐的突起吓退掠食者（威瓦西亚虫、怪诞虫）。

entries.k: Sheltering eggs and fry in the mouth (cichlids).
entries.v: 把卵和鱼苗含在口中保护（慈鲷）。

entries.k: Sheltering in a den through the cold months (bears).
entries.v: 在巢穴中度过寒冷的月份（熊）。

entries.k: Shorebirds probe mud with long bills.
Short trips out of the water onto land.
Shoulder and hip girdles strong enough to carry the body out of water.
entries.v: 肩带和腰带强壮到足以在水外支撑身体。

entries.k: Showing size and colour to settle disputes without fighting.
entries.v: 展示体型和颜色，不战而解决争端。

entries.k: Showing that you give up, so the winner stops attacking.
entries.v: 表示认输，使胜者停止攻击。

entries.k: Showing the young how to do things on purpose.
entries.v: 有意识地示范给幼崽如何做事。
西伯利亚暗色岩开始喷发

entries.k: Siberian Traps eruptions trigger the Permian–Triassic extinction (~252 Ma): ~80% of marine species lost
entries.v: 西伯利亚暗色岩喷发引发二叠纪–三叠纪大灭绝（约 252 Ma）：约 80% 的海洋物种消失

entries.k: Sitting on the eggs to keep them warm.
Sitting out the cold or dry season in a resting state.
entries.v: 以休眠状态度过寒季或旱季。
六层皮层带来灵活的行为（哺乳动物）。

entries.k: Sizing each other up and grappling with claws (crustaceans, scorpions).
entries.v: 互相打量并用螯钳扭打（甲壳类、蝎子）。
产生毒素的皮肤腺体（两栖类）。

entries.k: Skin, scales, feathers, fur, colour and armour.
entries.v: 皮肤、鳞片、羽毛、皮毛、颜色与护甲。

entries.k: Sleep, shelter, dormancy and saving energy.

entries.v: 在飞行中睡觉（雨燕、军舰鸟）。

entries.k: Sleeping inside a bubble of mucus (parrotfish, lungfish).
entries.v: 在黏液泡中睡觉（鹦嘴鱼、肺鱼）。

entries.k: Sleeping through droughts, like lungfish in mud cocoons.
entries.v: 在干旱中休眠，就像泥茧中的肺鱼。
大量个体聚在一起睡觉。

entries.k: Slender early theropod from Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
entries.v: 来自新墨西哥州幽灵牧场的纤细早期兽脚类。

entries.k: Slender flies whose larvae filter-feed in still water while the adults sip nectar; only females take blood, to fuel their eggs. The oldest known mosquitoes are preserved in Cretaceous amber about 99 million years old.
entries.v: 身体纤细的双翅昆虫，幼虫在静水中滤食，成虫吸食花蜜；只有雌蚊吸血，为产卵提供养分。已知最古老的蚊子保存在约9900万年前的白垩纪琥珀中。

entries.k: Slippery slime that protects the skin and eases movement.
entries.v: 滑溜的黏液，保护皮肤并使运动更顺畅。

entries.k: Slits in the throat that let water flow out past the gills.
entries.v: 喉部的裂缝，让水流经鳃后排出。

entries.k: Slow growth gives time for a bigger brain to develop.
entries.v: 缓慢的生长为更大的大脑发育争取时间。

entries.k: Slow-wave sleep that restores the brain.
entries.v: 让大脑恢复的慢波睡眠。

entries.k: Small Eocene deer-like animal from Kashmir, a close relative of the first whales.
entries.v: 来自克什米尔的小型始新世鹿状动物，与最早的鲸类亲缘很近。

entries.k: Small feathered plant-eating dinosaur from Transbaikalia.
entries.v: 来自外贝加尔的小型带羽植食恐龙。

entries.k: Small pachypleurosaur reptile of the Guizhou seas, bearing live young.
entries.v: 贵州海域的小型肿肋龙类爬行动物，胎生。

entries.k: Small proteins that punch holes in bacteria.
entries.v: 在细菌上打孔的小型蛋白质。

entries.k: Small vascular plants along wet lowlands
entries.v: 潮湿低地沿岸的小型维管植物

entries.k: Smell and taste: detecting dissolved chemicals.
entries.v: 嗅觉与味觉：探测溶解的化学物质。

entries.k: Soldiers, workers and nurses, each built for its job.
entries.v: 兵蚁、工蚁和保育者，各自为其职责而生。

entries.k: Songbirds learn their songs; lyrebirds mimic almost anything.
entries.v: 鸣禽通过学习掌握鸣唱；琴鸟几乎什么声音都能模仿。
模仿成年个体学会的歌（鸣禽）。

entries.k: South and Central America, the Caribbean and southern Florida.
entries.v: 南美洲和中美洲、加勒比地区以及佛罗里达南部。

entries.k: Spawning together on a cue from the moon or temperature.
entries.v: 依据月相或温度信号同时产卵。

entries.k: Sperm is delivered inside the female.
Sperm packets left for the female to pick up.
entries.v: 留给雌性拾取的精子包。

entries.k: Spiny lobopodian worm from the Burgess Shale.
entries.v: 布尔吉斯页岩中长刺的叶足动物。

entries.k: Splashing in water to clean feathers or fur.
entries.v: 在水中扑腾以清洁羽毛或皮毛。

entries.k: Sponge-like animals that built the first animal reefs, along the Lena River.
entries.v: 沿勒拿河建造了最早动物礁的类海绵动物。

entries.k: Sporozoans are parasites that enter their hosts' cells with a complex at their tip.
entries.v: 孢子虫是寄生虫，靠顶端的一套复合结构侵入宿主细胞。
喷射刺激性物质（放屁虫，后来的臭鼬）。

entries.k: Spreading fins, gaping or rearing up to look bigger instead of fighting.
entries.v: 张开鳍、张大嘴或直立起来显得更大，以代替争斗。

entries.k: Spring-fed pool ringed with microbial mats
entries.v: 微生物席环绕的泉水池

entries.k: Spring-fed pool with Calamites and tree ferns
entries.v: 泉水池，伴有芦木与树蕨

entries.k: Spring-fed pool with cycads and tree ferns
entries.v: 泉水池，伴有苏铁与树蕨

entries.k: Spring-fed pool with horsetails and mosses
entries.v: 泉水池，伴有木贼与苔藓

entries.k: Stacked gill plates (horseshoe crabs, sea scorpions).
Staying close to a mate to keep rivals away.
entries.v: 紧跟配偶，让对手无法靠近。

entries.k: Staying in and returning to a familiar area.
entries.v: 留在并返回熟悉的区域。

entries.k: Staying motionless so predators lose interest.
entries.v: 保持不动，使掠食者失去兴趣。

entries.k: Staying with one partner for a season or for life.
entries.v: 与同一伴侣相守一季或终生。

entries.k: Staying with the eggs to drive off egg-eaters.
Steering by the Earth's magnetic field.
Steering toward food and away from danger by following gradients.
entries.v: 沿着梯度趋向食物、远离危险。

entries.k: Sterile workers serve a breeding queen (termites, ants).
entries.v: 不育的工职个体侍奉一位繁殖的蚁后（白蚁、蚂蚁）。

entries.k: Stony corals, which first appear in the Middle Triassic and later build the Pacific atolls.
entries.v: 石珊瑚，最早出现于中三叠世，后来建造了太平洋的环礁。

entries.k: Stores urine and lets water be taken back (tetrapods).
entries.v: 储存尿液并重新吸收水分（四足动物）。

entries.k: Straightening and oiling feathers with the beak.
Subduing prey with venom (scorpions, later snakes).
entries.v: 用毒液制服猎物（蝎子，后来的蛇）。

entries.k: Sunbitterns flash eyespots on their wings.
entries.v: 日鳽展开翅膀亮出眼斑。
吞下的石头研磨食物（蜥脚类、鸟类）。

entries.k: Swarms take off together to settle new ground.
entries.v: 成群一起起飞，开拓新领地。

entries.k: Swimming in coordinated groups for safety.
entries.v: 为了安全而协调成群游动。

entries.k: Swinging between ~120 m below today and today's level
entries.v: 在比现今低约 120 m 与现今水平之间摆动

entries.k: Synapsids dominate: Dimetrodon, then therapsids (mammal ancestors)
entries.v: 合弓类占主导：先是异齿龙，后为兽孔类（哺乳动物的祖先）

entries.k: Tabulate and rugose corals, sponges and crinoids
entries.v: 床板珊瑚、四射珊瑚、海绵与海百合

entries.k: Tadpoles: amphibian young grow up in the water.
entries.v: 蝌蚪：两栖类幼体在水中长大。

entries.k: Talking with electric pulses (weakly electric fish).
Tapping signals through the ground or a web.
entries.v: 通过地面或蛛网敲击传递信号。

entries.k: Telling relatives from strangers by smell or sight.
entries.v: 凭气味或视觉区分亲属与陌生个体。

entries.k: Termites of northern Australia's tropical savannas that build earth mounds up to 8 metres tall, among the largest structures made by any animal besides humans. Soldiers defend the colony by squirting sticky glue from a pointed snout. Termites themselves date back to the Cretaceous.
entries.v: 生活在澳大利亚北部热带稀树草原的白蚁，建造高达8米的土丘，是除人类之外动物所建的最大结构之一。兵蚁从尖尖的吻部喷射黏胶来保卫蚁群。白蚁本身可追溯到白垩纪。

entries.k: Testate amoebae build shells around themselves, with an opening for their pseudopods.
entries.v: 有壳变形虫在自己周围建造外壳，留有一个开口供伪足伸出。

entries.k: Testosterone and oestrogen shape adult bodies.
entries.v: 睾酮与雌激素塑造成年体态。

entries.k: Tetrapods evolve from lobe-finned fish (Tiktaalik ~375 Ma, Acanthostega ~365 Ma)
entries.v: 四足动物由肉鳍鱼演化而来（提塔利克鱼约 375 Ma，棘螈约 365 Ma）

entries.k: The "giraffe camel" of the Middle and Late Miocene of North America, where camels first evolved. A humpless camel with very long, slender legs and a long neck, it held its small head about 3 m above the ground to browse on trees like a giraffe. Like modern camels it walked on padded feet with two toes.
entries.v: “长颈鹿骆驼”，生活在北美的中、晚中新世，而北美正是骆驼最早演化的地方。它是一种没有驼峰的骆驼，腿非常修长，脖子很长，小小的头部离地约3米，能像长颈鹿一样啃食树叶。和现代骆驼一样，它用带肉垫的双趾足行走。

entries.k: The "shovel-tusker", an elephant relative of the Middle Miocene of China, Mongolia and Kazakhstan, about 3 m tall. Its very long lower jaw ended in two broad, flat incisors forming a scoop, and a broad trunk rested on top of it. Once thought to shovel water plants, it is now thought to have cut and stripped branches and bark with the sharp edge of its scoop.
entries.v: “铲齿象”，一种来自中国、蒙古和哈萨克斯坦中中新世的象类近亲，身高约3米。它极长的下颌末端有两颗宽而扁平的门齿，组成一把铲子，宽阔的鼻子就搭在上面。人们曾认为它用来铲食水生植物，如今则认为它用铲子的锋利边缘切断树枝、剥下树皮。

entries.k: The "walking swimming whale" of the early Eocene of Pakistan, about 3 m long. It lived like a crocodile in estuaries and coastal rivers, with short legs, huge paddle-like hind feet and a long, powerful tail. It probably lurked in the shallows to ambush animals that came to drink, and could drink both fresh and salt water.
entries.v: 来自巴基斯坦早始新世的“会走路会游泳的鲸”，长约3米。它像鳄鱼一样生活在河口和沿海河流中，四肢短，后脚巨大如桨，尾巴长而有力。它可能潜伏在浅水中伏击前来饮水的动物，并且既能喝淡水也能喝咸水。

entries.k: The 'Age of Fishes'. The first forests transform the land and the atmosphere, and the first four-limbed vertebrates crawl ashore. Two extinction pulses end the period.
entries.v: “鱼类时代”。最早的森林改变了陆地和大气，最早的四肢脊椎动物爬上岸。两次灭绝脉冲终结了本纪。

entries.k: The 'crow shark', a mackerel shark about 2-3 metres long that swarmed the seas of the Late Cretaceous about 100-70 million years ago. Its curved, finely serrated teeth, like small saws, were good for cutting chunks out of carcasses. Its tooth marks and embedded teeth have been found on mosasaurs, sea turtles and even a duck-billed dinosaur washed out to sea, showing that it fed on anything it could find, dead or alive.
entries.v: 绰号“乌鸦鲨”，一种体长约2至3米的鼠鲨类，约1亿至7000万年前大量出没于晚白垩世的海洋。它弯曲的牙齿边缘有细密的锯齿，像小锯子一样，适合从尸体上切下肉块。在沧龙、海龟甚至一只被冲入大海的鸭嘴龙身上都发现了它的咬痕和嵌入的牙齿，说明它无论死活，见什么吃什么。

entries.k: The 'star ammonite' of the Early Jurassic seas, about 195 million years ago. Its loosely coiled shell, up to 20 cm across, has bold straight ribs and a sharp keel flanked by two grooves. Gas-filled chambers kept it buoyant while the animal hunted small prey with its arms. Its fossils are so common at Lyme Regis that a whole rock zone is named after it.
entries.v: 约1.95亿年前早侏罗世海洋中的“星菊石”。它松散盘卷的壳直径可达20厘米，有粗壮笔直的肋和两侧带沟的锐利腹棱。充气的气室使它保持浮力，动物则用腕捕捉小型猎物。它的化石在莱姆里吉斯极为常见，以至于整个岩层带都以它命名。

entries.k: The Asian cousin of Tyrannosaurus, about 10 metres long and 5 tonnes, that ruled the river plains of Mongolia about 70 million years ago. Its massive skull carried banana-sized teeth for a bone-crushing bite, while its arms were the smallest, relative to its body, of any tyrannosaur. It hunted the giant sauropods and duck-billed dinosaurs that lived alongside it.
entries.v: 霸王龙的亚洲近亲，体长约10米、重约5吨，约7000万年前称霸蒙古的河流平原。它巨大的头骨长着香蕉般大小的牙齿，咬合力足以咬碎骨头，而它的前肢相对身体而言是所有暴龙类中最小的。它捕食与它生活在一起的巨型蜥脚类和鸭嘴龙。

entries.k: The best-known plated dinosaur, about 9 metres long, from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of North America, about 155-150 million years old. Two staggered rows of broad bony plates ran down its arched back, probably for display, and four long spikes at the end of its tail made a formidable weapon. Its hind legs were far longer than its front legs, so it carried its tiny, narrow head close to the ground. It cropped low plants with a horny beak.
entries.v: 最著名的有板恐龙，体长约9米，来自约1.55亿-1.5亿年前北美的晚侏罗世莫里森组。两列交错排列的宽大骨板沿着它拱起的背部延伸，很可能用于展示；尾巴末端的四根长刺则构成了令人生畏的武器。它的后腿远长于前腿，因此细小狭窄的头部贴近地面。它用角质喙啃食低矮的植物。

entries.k: The best-known sea scorpion, from the Late Silurian of New York and Ontario, about 420 million years ago, and the state fossil of New York. Most individuals were 10-20 cm long. It swam with a pair of broad, paddle-shaped hind legs, caught small prey with its spiny front legs and had a long, slender, spike-like tail. Thousands of specimens are known from the shallow, salty lagoons of the Bertie Group.
entries.v: 最著名的海蝎，来自纽约州和安大略的晚志留世地层，距今约4.2亿年，也是纽约州的州化石。大多数个体长10-20厘米。它用一对宽阔的桨状后肢游泳，用多刺的前肢捕捉小型猎物，还有一条细长的尖刺状尾巴。在伯蒂群浅而咸的潟湖沉积中已发现数以千计的标本。

entries.k: The classic chain coral of Silurian seas, first named by Linnaeus and best known from Gotland, Sweden. Its colonies were built of walls one tube thick, made of oval corallites about 2 mm across, which joined and branched to enclose open windows of very variable size, often long and arranged in rough parallel rows. Colonies grew to tens of centimetres across and were common in Silurian reefs and coral beds.
entries.v: 志留纪海洋中最典型的链珊瑚，最早由林奈命名，以瑞典哥得兰岛的化石最为著名。它的群体由单层管壁构成，每道壁是一排直径约2毫米的椭圆形珊瑚个体，这些壁相互连接、分叉，围出大小差异很大的空窗，窗孔常呈长条形并大致平行排列。群体可宽达数十厘米，在志留纪的礁体和珊瑚层中十分常见。

entries.k: The Indian subcontinent, Indochina, southern China and the Sunda islands (also called Indomalayan).
entries.v: 印度次大陆、中南半岛、华南和巽他群岛（又称印度-马来界）。

entries.k: The commonest animal of the Burgess Shale of British Columbia, about 508 million years old, known from tens of thousands of specimens and the first fossil Charles Walcott collected there in 1909. Under 2 cm long, it had a small head shield with two pairs of long spines sweeping back over its body, a pair of long antennae and a pair of bristly swimming antennae. Its 26 body segments each bore a leg and a feathery gill branch, and it probably swam just above the mud picking up food particles.
entries.v: 不列颠哥伦比亚省伯吉斯页岩中最常见的动物，距今约5.08亿年，已知标本达数万件，也是查尔斯·沃尔科特1909年在那里采集的第一件化石。它体长不到2厘米，有一块小小的头盾，头盾上两对长刺向后掠过身体，还有一对长触角和一对长有刚毛的游泳触角。它的26个体节各有一条腿和一根羽状鳃枝，它很可能在泥面上方游动，拾取食物颗粒。

entries.k: The commonest cephalopod of the Early and Middle Ordovician seas of Baltica, so abundant that a Scandinavian limestone was once named after it. An endocerid, it had a long, smooth, straight shell probably a metre or more long, with a wide tube along the belly filled with stacked cone-shaped deposits that acted as ballast. Big, heavily built and hard to kill, it cruised slowly over the sea floor hunting trilobites and other prey.
entries.v: 奥陶纪早中期波罗的古陆海洋中最常见的头足类，数量之多，以至于斯堪的纳维亚的一种石灰岩曾以它命名。它属于内角石类，长而光滑的直壳可能长达一米或更长，腹侧有一条宽管，里面叠满锥状沉积物，起到压舱作用。它体形庞大、结构厚重、极难杀死，在海底上方缓缓巡游，捕食三叶虫等猎物。

entries.k: The commonest large predator of the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of the western United States, about 155-150 million years old. Adults reached about 8.5 metres, with a long, narrow skull bearing a short horn in front of each eye and a low ridge along each side of the snout. Rather than a crushing bite, it probably struck with its upper jaw like a hatchet, slicing with serrated teeth. Wounds on Stegosaurus and Allosaurus bones record fights between the two.
entries.v: 美国西部晚侏罗世莫里森组中最常见的大型掠食者，距今约1.55亿至1.5亿年。成体体长约8.5米，长而窄的头骨上每只眼睛前方都有一个短角，吻部两侧各有一条低矮的脊。它可能并非靠压碎式撕咬，而是像挥斧头一样用上颌猛击，用锯齿状牙齿切割猎物。剑龙和异特龙骨骼上的伤痕记录了两者之间的搏斗。

entries.k: The commonest radiodont of the Chengjiang biota of Yunnan, China, about 518 million years old, and a close relative of Anomalocaris. Each frontal appendage carried one enormous forward spine that closed against the rest of the limb like the jaw of a pair of pincers. It swam with eleven pairs of body flaps and had a long tail fan with streamers; a 2023 study of its growth suggests the biggest individuals were well over half a metre long.
entries.v: 中国云南澄江生物群中最常见的放射齿类，距今约5.18亿年，是奇虾的近亲。每条前附肢上都长着一根向前伸出的巨大棘刺，能与附肢其余部分合拢，就像一把钳子的钳口。它靠十一对身体桨叶游泳，还有一条带飘带的长尾扇；2023年一项关于其生长的研究表明，最大的个体体长远超过半米。

entries.k: The deadliest malaria parasite, a sporozoan that lives inside the red blood cells of people and multiplies there, bursting them in waves of fever. Its life alternates between humans and Anopheles mosquitoes, which pick up its crescent-shaped sexual stages with a meal of blood and pass it on with their next bite. It descends from a parasite of gorillas, which crossed over to humans in Africa, and has shaped human history and even the human genome.
entries.v: 最致命的疟原虫，是一种孢子虫，生活在人类红细胞内并在其中增殖，使红细胞破裂，引发一阵阵发热。它的生活史在人类和按蚊之间交替：按蚊吸血时吸入它新月形的有性阶段，并在下一次叮咬时把它传播出去。它起源于一种大猩猩的寄生虫，这种寄生虫在非洲传给了人类；它塑造了人类历史，甚至影响了人类的基因组。

entries.k: The earliest known diapsid reptile, the lineage that later gave rise to lizards, crocodiles and dinosaurs, from Late Carboniferous rocks near Garnett, Kansas, about 302 million years old. It was a slender animal some 40 cm long, with a small head, a long neck, long legs and a tail longer than the rest of its body. It probably darted through the undergrowth of the coal forests hunting insects and other small invertebrates.
entries.v: 已知最早的双孔类爬行动物——这一支系后来演化出蜥蜴、鳄类和恐龙——发现于美国堪萨斯州加尼特附近的晚石炭世岩层，距今约3.02亿年。它体形纤细，长约40厘米，头小、颈长、腿长，尾巴比身体其余部分还长。它可能在煤炭森林的林下灌丛中穿梭，捕食昆虫和其他小型无脊椎动物。

entries.k: The fastest land animal of the Americas, a deer-sized runner of the western prairies and deserts that can sprint at about 90 km/h and keep up 50 to 70 km/h for several kilometres. It is the last survivor of a family once rich in species and not a true antelope; its forked horn sheaths are shed every year. Its huge eyes spot danger kilometres away, and its speed may have evolved to escape the cheetah-like cats of Ice Age North America.
entries.v: 美洲跑得最快的陆生动物，是生活在北美西部草原和荒漠中的一种鹿般大小的奔跑者，冲刺速度约每小时90千米，还能以每小时50到70千米的速度连续奔跑数千米。它是一个曾经物种繁多的科的最后幸存者，并非真正的羚羊；它的分叉角鞘每年都会脱落。它巨大的眼睛能在数千米外发现危险，而它的速度或许是为了逃避冰河时代北美类似猎豹的猫科动物而演化出来的。

entries.k: The first known burrowing dinosaur, a small plant-eater about 2 metres long from Montana and Idaho about 95 million years ago. It was found curled up with two half-grown young at the end of a sloping, S-shaped burrow, the first evidence of a dinosaur digging dens and caring for its offspring. Its strong snout, shoulders and hips helped it dig, and a burrow offered shelter from predators and the weather.
entries.v: 已知第一种会挖洞的恐龙，一种体长约2米的小型植食恐龙，约9500万年前生活在蒙大拿和爱达荷。它被发现时与两只半大的幼崽一起蜷缩在一条倾斜的S形洞穴尽头，这是恐龙挖掘巢穴并照顾后代的首个证据。它强壮的吻部、肩部和臀部有助于挖掘，洞穴能为它遮挡掠食者和恶劣天气。

entries.k: The largest amphibian known, perhaps 5.5 to 9 metres long, from the Early Permian rivers and lakes of north-eastern Brazil, around 275 million years ago. It looked much like a giant gharial, with an extremely long, narrow snout lined with sharp teeth, a long, low body and a powerful swimming tail. It lay in wait in the water and snapped up fish and other animals with a sideways sweep of its jaws. Its sheer size made it both a deadly ambusher and very hard to kill.
entries.v: 已知最大的两栖动物，体长可能达 5.5 至 9 米，生活在约 2.75 亿年前二叠纪早期巴西东北部的河流与湖泊中。它的外形很像一条巨型长吻鳄，极长而狭窄的吻部排满尖牙，身体长而低矮，尾巴强健善游。它潜伏在水中，猛地侧甩双颌咬住鱼类和其他动物。庞大的体型使它既是致命的伏击者，又极难被杀死。

entries.k: The largest ant known, from the warm early Eocene forests of Germany; its winged queens were about 6 cm long with a 15 cm wingspan, as big as a hummingbird. It lived only where the climate was tropical. Each ant was weak, but huge colonies swarmed over prey and rivals together.
entries.v: 已知最大的蚂蚁，生活在德国温暖的早始新世森林中；它有翅的蚁后体长约6厘米，翼展15厘米，和蜂鸟一样大。它只生活在气候炎热的热带地区。单只蚂蚁很弱小，但庞大的蚁群会一拥而上，共同对付猎物和对手。

entries.k: The largest brachiopod that ever lived, with a shell up to about 30 centimetres wide, from the warm, shallow Early Carboniferous seas of Europe, Asia and North Africa, about 335 million years ago. It lay on the sea floor in a huge, thick, strongly curved shell, much wider than long, and fed by filtering food particles from the water through the gaping front of its shell. Its massive shell made it almost impossible for predators to break.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的腕足动物，壳宽可达约30厘米，生活在约3.35亿年前欧洲、亚洲和北非温暖的早石炭世浅海中。它躺在海底一个巨大、厚实、强烈弯曲的壳里，壳宽远大于长，通过壳前端张开的缝隙滤食水中的食物颗粒。厚重的贝壳使掠食者几乎不可能将其打破。

entries.k: The largest complete trilobite ever found: the holotype, from Late Ordovician rocks near Churchill in northern Manitoba, is 72 cm long. Its smooth, elongate oval shield lacks cheek spines. It lived in warm, shallow tropical seas and probably ploughed through the seafloor sediment hunting and scavenging soft-bodied prey.
entries.v: 迄今发现的最大的完整三叶虫：其正模标本出自加拿大马尼托巴省北部丘吉尔附近的晚奥陶世岩层，体长72厘米。它的背甲光滑、呈长椭圆形，没有颊刺。它生活在温暖的热带浅海中，可能在海底沉积物中犁行，捕食或拾取软体猎物。

entries.k: The Late Paleozoic Ice Age ends in the early Permian
entries.v: 晚古生代冰期于二叠纪早期结束

entries.k: The North and South China blocks and Indochina, islands in the Paleo-Tethys.
entries.v: 华北、华南地块及印支地块，古特提斯系中的岛屿。

entries.k: The largest entelodont or "hell pig", about 1.8 m tall at the shoulder, from the latest Oligocene and Early Miocene of North America. Its huge head had bony flanges under the cheeks and knobs under the chin, and its teeth could crack bones. Entelodonts were not true pigs but relatives of whales and hippos; Daeodon probably scavenged carcasses and ate roots and fruit.
entries.v: 最大的完齿猪类，即“地狱猪”，肩高约1.8米，生活在北美洲最晚渐新世和早中新世。它巨大的头部在颊部下方有骨质凸缘，下巴下方有骨瘤，牙齿能够咬碎骨头。完齿猪类并非真正的猪，而是鲸和河马的近亲；恐颌猪可能以动物尸体为食，也吃植物根茎和果实。

entries.k: The largest glyptodont, about 3.6 m long and up to 1.5 tonnes, from Pleistocene South America; it died out about 11,000 years ago. Its tall domed shell of fused bony plates was nearly impossible to bite through, and its long armoured tail ended in a massive club studded with spikes. Cracked shells of other Doedicurus suggest rivals clubbed each other, and a blow could break a predator's bones.
entries.v: 最大的雕齿兽，体长约3.6米，体重可达1.5吨，生活在更新世的南美洲，约11000年前灭绝。它由骨板愈合而成的高拱甲壳几乎不可能被咬穿，长长的披甲尾巴末端是一个布满尖刺的巨大尾锤。其他星尾兽甲壳上的裂痕表明，对手之间会用尾锤互相击打，这样的一击足以打断捕食者的骨头。

entries.k: The largest hyena that ever lived, about lion-sized at up to 110 kg, ranging across Africa and Eurasia from the Late Pliocene to the Middle Pleistocene. Its short, broad muzzle and huge teeth gave it a bone-cracking bite, and it probably stole kills from sabre-toothed cats as well as hunting for itself. It lived and fought in clans.
entries.v: 史上最大的鬣狗，体型与狮子相当，体重可达110千克，从晚上新世到中更新世分布于非洲和欧亚大陆。它短而宽的口鼻和巨大的牙齿能咬碎骨头，除了自己捕猎，它很可能还从剑齿虎口中抢夺猎物。它们以家族群体生活和战斗。

entries.k: The largest insect known, a griffinfly with a wingspan of about 71 centimetres from the Early Permian of Kansas and Oklahoma, around 275 million years ago. Like its Carboniferous relative Meganeura it was a giant cousin of modern dragonflies, catching other insects in flight with its spiny legs. It had a slightly longer body and narrower wings than Meganeura. Its size may have been possible because the air of the time was richer in oxygen than today.
entries.v: 已知最大的昆虫，一种翼展约71厘米的巨脉蜻蜓，生活在约2.75亿年前早二叠世的堪萨斯和俄克拉何马。与石炭纪的近亲巨脉蜻蜓属一样，它是现代蜻蜓的巨型远亲，用多刺的足在飞行中捕捉其他昆虫。它的身体比巨脉蜻蜓属略长，翅膀更窄。它能长得如此之大，可能是因为当时空气中的氧气比今天更丰富。

entries.k: The largest known hadrosaur and the biggest ornithopod of all, about 15 metres long and some 13-16 tonnes, from the floodplains of Shandong in China about 72 million years ago. It had a long, flat, crestless head with a broad duck-bill and some 1,500 grinding teeth. It lived in large herds, and its great size made adults hard for even tyrannosaurs to bring down.
entries.v: 已知最大的鸭嘴龙，也是所有鸟脚类中最大的，体长约15米、重约13至16吨，约7200万年前生活在中国山东的泛滥平原上。它长着又长又平、没有头冠的脑袋，宽阔的鸭嘴后面有约1500颗研磨用的牙齿。它们成大群生活，巨大的体型让即使是暴龙也很难撂倒成年个体。

entries.k: The largest known lobe-finned fish, a rhizodont from Early Carboniferous rivers and lagoons of Scotland, about 335 million years ago, estimated at up to about 7 metres long. Its jaws carried enormous fangs, some about 22 cm long, and it had big fleshy pectoral fins. It was the top predator of its waters and could probably catch large fish and even early tetrapods venturing into the shallows.
entries.v: 已知最大的肉鳍鱼，是一种根齿鱼类，生活在约3.35亿年前苏格兰早石炭世的河流和潟湖中，估计体长可达约7米。它的颌部长着巨大的獠牙，有的长约22厘米，还有肉质发达的大胸鳍。它是所在水域的顶级掠食者，很可能能够捕捉大型鱼类，甚至是闯入浅水的早期四足动物。

entries.k: The largest known raptor, a feathered dromaeosaurid about 6 metres long and up to half a tonne, from Utah about 135 million years ago. Each foot carried a sickle claw some 24 cm long, and it was stockier and more powerful than its smaller relatives. A block of rock holding several Utahraptors of different ages suggests they may have hunted or gathered in groups.
entries.v: 已知最大的驰龙类，一种长有羽毛的恐龙，体长约6米、重可达半吨，生活在约1.35亿年前的犹他州。每只脚上都有一个长约24厘米的镰刀状爪，体格比它的小型亲戚粗壮有力得多。一块保存着多只不同年龄犹他盗龙的岩块表明，它们可能成群狩猎或聚集。

entries.k: The largest known relative of mammals that was not itself a mammal: an elephant-sized dicynodont about 4.5 metres long and weighing about 9 tonnes, from Poland about 210 million years ago. Unlike earlier dicynodonts it stood on straight, pillar-like legs, and it cropped plants with a toothless horny beak flanked by two short tusks. Its sheer bulk made it very hard for any predator to bring down.
entries.v: 已知最大的非哺乳类哺乳动物亲戚：一种大象般大小的二齿兽，体长约4.5米，体重约9吨，约2.1亿年前生活在波兰。与早期二齿兽不同，它用笔直如柱的四肢站立，用两侧长着短獠牙的无齿角质喙啃食植物。庞大的体型让任何掠食者都很难将它击倒。

entries.k: The largest land tortoise known, with a shell about 2 metres long, living from Pakistan and India to Southeast Asia from the Late Miocene to the Pleistocene. It plodded on elephant-like legs, browsing low plants, and when threatened it could draw its scaly limbs and head in under a domed shell that almost no predator could break. It was extremely slow.
entries.v: 已知最大的陆龟，背甲长约2米，从晚中新世到更新世分布于巴基斯坦、印度直至东南亚。它迈着象腿般的四肢缓慢行走，啃食低矮的植物；受到威胁时，它能把覆满鳞片的四肢和头缩进高拱的龟壳，几乎没有捕食者能打破这层甲壳。它行动极其缓慢。

entries.k: The largest marsupial that ever lived, a wombat relative the size of a hippopotamus, weighing up to 2.7 tonnes. It roamed the open woodlands and grasslands of Pleistocene Australia, and fossils suggest it migrated with the seasons. Like other marsupials it carried its young in a pouch; it died out about 40,000 years ago, after people reached Australia.
entries.v: 有史以来最大的有袋类，是袋熊的亲属，体型与河马相当，体重可达2.7吨。它漫游于更新世澳大利亚开阔的林地和草原，化石表明它会随季节迁徙。和其他有袋类一样，它把幼崽放在育儿袋里；它在大约4万年前、人类到达澳大利亚之后灭绝。

entries.k: The largest mosasaur, a giant marine lizard related to monitor lizards and snakes, about 11-13 metres long, from the seas of the last few million years of the Cretaceous, about 70-66 million years ago. It had massive jaws with thick conical teeth, four paddle limbs and a tail with a shark-like fluke. It was a top predator that ate fish, turtles, ammonites and other marine reptiles. A skull found near Maastricht in the Netherlands in the 1770s was one of the first fossils recognised as an extinct animal.
entries.v: 最大的沧龙类，一种与巨蜥和蛇有亲缘关系的巨型海生蜥蜴，体长约11-13米，生活在白垩纪最后几百万年的海洋中，距今约7000万-6600万年。它有巨大的颌部和粗壮的圆锥形牙齿、四个桨状肢以及末端带有鲨鱼般尾叶的尾巴。它是顶级掠食者，以鱼类、海龟、菊石和其他海生爬行动物为食。18世纪70年代在荷兰马斯特里赫特附近发现的一具头骨，是最早被认定为已灭绝动物的化石之一。

entries.k: The largest of the teleosaurids, marine relatives of crocodiles, reaching about 7 metres in the coastal seas and lagoons of Late Jurassic Europe. Its broad, robust snout carried short, blunt teeth built to crack turtle shells and hard-bodied prey. Unlike the smooth-skinned metriorhynchids, it kept thick rows of bony armour on its back and belly, making it both a crushing biter and hard to wound.
entries.v: 体型最大的真蜥鳄类，是鳄类的海生亲戚，体长约7米，生活在晚侏罗世欧洲的沿海和潟湖中。它宽阔粗壮的吻部长着短而钝的牙齿，专门用来咬碎龟壳和硬壳猎物。与皮肤光滑的地蜥鳄类不同，它的背部和腹部仍保留着厚厚的成排骨甲，既能咬碎猎物，又很难被伤到。

entries.k: The largest pangolin, up to about 1.8 m long with its tail and over 30 kg, living in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa. Its body is covered in large, overlapping scales of keratin, and when attacked it rolls into a tight ball that even lions struggle to open. At night it tears into termite mounds and ant nests with its huge front claws and licks up the insects with a very long, sticky tongue.
entries.v: 最大的穿山甲，连尾巴体长可达约1.8米，体重超过30千克，生活在赤道非洲的森林和稀树草原。它全身覆盖着大块相互交叠的角质鳞片，遇到攻击时会蜷成一个紧实的球，连狮子都很难把它掰开。夜里，它用巨大的前爪扒开白蚁丘和蚁巢，再用极长的黏舌舔食昆虫。

entries.k: The largest rodent ever found, a bull-sized relative of the pacarana from the Pliocene of Uruguay, about 3 m long and perhaps half a tonne to a tonne in weight. It lived in the forested deltas of the ancient Rio de la Plata, feeding on soft plants. Its enormous incisors could bite as hard as a tiger's, for digging and for fighting off predators, and its sheer bulk made it very hard to kill.
entries.v: 迄今发现的最大啮齿动物，是乌拉圭上新世一种体型如公牛的长尾豚鼠近亲，体长约3米，体重或许半吨到一吨。它生活在古拉普拉塔河森林茂密的三角洲，以柔软的植物为食。它巨大的门齿咬合力可与老虎相比，可用来挖掘和抵御捕食者，庞大的身躯也让它极难被杀死。

entries.k: The largest snake ever found, a relative of boas and anacondas from the middle to late Paleocene of Colombia, about 13 m long and weighing over a tonne. It lived in the hot rainforest rivers of the Cerrejon Formation a few million years after the dinosaurs died out, and probably hunted fish and crocodile relatives. Its size suggests the tropics were then several degrees warmer than today.
entries.v: 已发现的最大的蛇，是蚺和水蚺的亲属，来自哥伦比亚古新世中晚期，体长约13米，体重超过1吨。它生活在恐龙灭绝几百万年后塞雷洪组炎热的雨林河流中，可能以鱼类和鳄类的亲属为食。它的体型表明，当时热带地区比现在要温暖好几度。

entries.k: The largest turtle known, about 4.6 metres long and over 2 tonnes, from the inland sea of North America about 80-74 million years ago. Its broad shell was a framework of bony ribs probably covered in tough leathery skin, like that of today's leatherback, and its front flippers spanned about 4 metres. It probably fed on soft-bodied prey such as jellyfish and squid and on shelled ammonites, which its hooked beak could crack.
entries.v: 已知最大的龟，体长约4.6米，体重超过2吨，来自约8000万-7400万年前的北美内陆海。它宽阔的甲壳是由骨质肋骨构成的框架，很可能像今天的棱皮龟一样覆盖着坚韧的革质皮肤，前鳍肢展开约4米。它很可能以水母和乌贼等软体猎物为食，也吃有壳的菊石，它的钩状喙可以啄碎菊石壳。

entries.k: The largest well-known ostrich dinosaur, about 6 metres long and 400 kg, from Mongolia about 70 million years ago. It had a small toothless beak, large eyes, a long neck and very long legs built for speed, and may have run at 40-60 km/h. Many skeletons of different ages found together suggest it lived in groups, relying on speed rather than weapons to escape predators.
entries.v: 已知最大的似鸟龙类之一，体长约6米、重约400公斤，约7000万年前生活在蒙古。它有小而无牙的喙、大眼睛、长脖子和适合奔跑的长腿，奔跑速度可能达到每小时40至60公里。许多不同年龄的骨骼一起被发现，说明它们成群生活，依靠速度而不是武器逃避掠食者。

entries.k: The namesake of the gorgonopsians, a sabre-toothed predator about 2 metres long from the Late Permian Karoo of South Africa, around 258 million years ago. Its long skull held long, blade-like upper canines and could open in a huge gape to drive them into prey. Its legs were held more upright than in earlier synapsids, making it an agile hunter of dicynodonts and pareiasaurs. Gorgonopsians were the top predators of the Late Permian until they vanished in the end-Permian mass extinction.
entries.v: 丽齿兽类的名称来源，一种体长约2米的剑齿掠食者，来自南非晚二叠世的卡鲁盆地，距今约2.58亿年。它狭长的头骨上长着刀刃般的长上犬齿，嘴巴能张得极大，将犬齿刺入猎物。它的四肢比早期合弓纲动物更为直立，使它成为捕食二齿兽类和锯齿龙类的敏捷猎手。丽齿兽类是晚二叠世的顶级掠食者，直到在二叠纪末大灭绝中消失。

entries.k: The oldest known gliding mammal, a squirrel-sized animal from the Daohugou beds of Inner Mongolia, about 164-159 million years old. A furry skin membrane stretched between its front and hind limbs, preserved with hair impressions, and its long, flattened tail acted as a stabiliser. It belonged to the eutriconodonts, an extinct group of early mammals. Its sharp, pointed teeth suggest a diet of insects.
entries.v: 已知最古老的滑翔哺乳动物，一种松鼠大小的动物，来自内蒙古的道虎沟化石层，距今约1.64亿-1.59亿年。前后肢之间伸展着一层毛茸茸的皮膜，保存有毛发印痕，而长而扁平的尾巴起到稳定作用。它属于真三尖齿兽类，这是一类已灭绝的早期哺乳动物。它尖锐的牙齿表明它以昆虫为食。

entries.k: The oldest known harvestman, from the hot-spring wetlands of Rhynie in Scotland, about 410 million years ago. It already looked remarkably like living harvestmen, with a compact oval body only a few millimetres long, a pair of eyes on a central bump and four pairs of very long, thin legs. Those stilt-like legs carried it quickly over the ground as it searched for small prey and decaying scraps.
entries.v: 已知最古老的盲蛛，来自约4.1亿年前苏格兰莱尼的温泉湿地。它的样子已与现生盲蛛惊人地相似：紧凑的椭圆形身体只有几毫米长，中央的小丘上有一对眼睛，还有四对又长又细的腿。这些高跷般的长腿载着它在地面上快速移动，寻找小型猎物和腐烂的碎屑。

entries.k: The oldest known horseshoe crab, from Late Ordovician shallow-marine rocks in Manitoba, Canada, about 445 million years ago. It was only about 4 cm long, with a large crescent-shaped head shield bearing small eyes, a segmented abdomen and a long, spear-like tail spine. Its body plan already resembled that of living horseshoe crabs, which have changed remarkably little since.
entries.v: 已知最古老的鲎，产自加拿大马尼托巴省约4.45亿年前的晚奥陶世浅海岩层。它体长仅约4厘米，有一块带小眼的新月形大头甲、分节的腹部和一根长矛状的长尾剑。它的身体结构已与现生鲎相似，而现生鲎自那以后几乎没有什么变化。

entries.k: The oldest well-described sea scorpion, from the Middle Ordovician (Darriwilian) Winneshiek Shale of Iowa, about 467 million years ago. Estimated at up to 1.7 m long, it was one of the largest predators of its time. Its name recalls the penteconter, a Greek warship. Like other megalograptids it caught prey with long, spiny front legs and swam with paddle-shaped hind legs; it lived in a brackish coastal inlet.
entries.v: 已得到充分描述的最古老板足鲎，来自美国艾奥瓦州中奥陶世（达瑞威尔期）的温尼希克页岩，距今约4.67亿年。据估计其体长可达1.7米，是当时最大的掠食者之一。其名源自古希腊战船"五十桨船"。与其他巨翅鲎类一样，它用长而多刺的前肢捕捉猎物，用桨状后肢游泳；它生活在半咸水的沿海海湾中。

entries.k: The oldest well-preserved sea spider, from the Herefordshire Lagerstaette of England, about 430 million years ago; its body was only a few millimetres long. It had four pairs of long, jointed legs on a slender trunk, a long proboscis, a big pair of claws at the front and, unlike living sea spiders, a long segmented tail. Like its living relatives it probably fed on soft-bodied animals such as sponges and hydroids.
entries.v: 保存完好的最古老海蜘蛛，来自英格兰的赫里福德郡化石库，距今约4.3亿年；它的身体只有几毫米长。它细长的躯干上长着四对有关节的长腿，还有一根长长的吻、前端一对大螯，而且与现生海蜘蛛不同，它有一条分节的长尾。像现生近亲一样，它可能以海绵和水螅等软体动物为食。

entries.k: The only large Ordovician horn coral, common in the Late Ordovician seas of Kentucky, Indiana, Ohio and Ontario. Each polyp lived alone in a thick, curved, cone-shaped skeleton usually 4-8 cm and up to 13 cm long, lying on the soft sea floor; its deep cup was lined with many crowded ridges whose inner ends twisted together into a raised knot in the middle. Its heavy skeleton made it very hard to damage, and old shells often became homes for encrusting bryozoans.
entries.v: 奥陶纪唯一的大型角珊瑚，常见于美国肯塔基、印第安纳、俄亥俄和加拿大安大略的奥陶纪晚期海洋中。每个珊瑚虫独自生活在一个厚实、弯曲的锥形骨骼里，骨骼通常长4-8厘米，最长可达13厘米，平躺在松软的海底；深深的杯腔内排列着许多密集的隔壁，其内端在中央扭结成一个隆起的轴部构造。厚重的骨骼使它极难受损，老骨骼还常常成为结壳苔藓虫的家园。

entries.k: The original honeycomb coral, first described from Silurian rocks of Gotland, Sweden. Its domed or lumpy colonies were made of thousands of thin-walled, many-sided tubes about 2-3 mm wide, packed together like the cells of a honeycomb and linked by tiny pores in their walls. It was a common reef builder in Silurian seas from Estonia and Scandinavia to Britain.
entries.v: 蜂巢珊瑚的模式种，最早根据瑞典哥得兰岛志留纪地层的化石描述。它的群体呈圆丘状或块状，由成千上万根宽约2–3毫米的薄壁多边形管紧密排列而成，宛如蜂巢，管壁上的细小壁孔将相邻个体相连。它是志留纪海洋中常见的造礁生物，分布于爱沙尼亚、斯堪的纳维亚至英国。

entries.k: The Siberian craton, later the heart of Angaraland and the Siberian Traps.
entries.v: 西伯利亚克拉通，后来成为安加拉古陆和西伯利亚暗色岩的核心。

entries.k: The amniotic egg freed reptiles from the water.
entries.v: 羊膜卵让爬行动物摆脱了对水的依赖。

entries.k: The ancient core of North America, straddling the equator in the early Paleozoic.
entries.v: 北美洲的古老核心，在早古生代横跨赤道。

entries.k: The bird with the longest wingspan alive, over three metres. It can glide for hours over the Southern Ocean without flapping, feeding on squid and fish, and returns to sub-Antarctic islands to raise a single chick every two years.
entries.v: 现存翼展最长的鸟类，超过三米。它能在南大洋上空不扇动翅膀滑翔数小时，以鱿鱼和鱼类为食，每两年回到亚南极岛屿养育一只雏鸟。

entries.k: The body is built from repeated segments that can specialise independently.
entries.v: 身体由重复的体节构成，各体节可独立特化。

entries.k: The earliest known reptile, a small lizard-like animal about 20 cm long from the coal forests of Nova Scotia, 312 million years ago. Its fossils were found inside the hollow stumps of giant lycopsid trees, where it may have hunted insects and millipedes. Like later reptiles it probably laid shelled eggs on land.
entries.v: 已知最早的爬行动物，一种约20厘米长、形似蜥蜴的小动物，生活在3.12亿年前新斯科舍的煤炭森林中。它的化石发现于巨型石松类树木中空的树桩里，它可能在那里捕食昆虫和千足虫。与后来的爬行动物一样，它可能在陆地上产下带壳的卵。

entries.k: The embryo is fed through the womb wall.
entries.v: 胚胎通过子宫壁获取营养。

entries.k: The first dinosaur ever named (1824), from Oxfordshire, England.
entries.v: 第一种被命名的恐龙（1824 年），来自英格兰牛津郡。

entries.k: The first pterosaur to be scientifically described, named in 1809 from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, about 150 million years old. Adults reached a wingspan of about one metre, with a long, narrow skull holding about 90 small teeth, a long neck and a very short tail. Some fossils preserve a low soft-tissue crest on the head. It probably hunted small fish and invertebrates around the lagoons of the Solnhofen islands.
entries.v: 第一种被科学描述的翼龙，1809年根据巴伐利亚约1.5亿年前晚侏罗世索伦霍芬石灰岩中的化石命名。成年个体翼展约一米，狭长的头骨中有约90颗小牙，颈长尾极短。一些化石保存了头顶低矮的软组织冠。它可能在索伦霍芬群岛的潟湖周围捕食小鱼和无脊椎动物。

entries.k: The first vertebrate kidney: a few tubules just behind the head.
entries.v: 最早的脊椎动物肾脏：头部后方的几条小管。

entries.k: The giraffe of Kenya and Tanzania, recognised by its jagged, vine-leaf-shaped dark patches. Bulls stand nearly 6 metres tall, the tallest of any living animal, and browse thorny acacias with a tongue up to 45 cm long. Like almost all mammals it has only seven neck vertebrae, each up to 25 cm long.
entries.v: 肯尼亚和坦桑尼亚的长颈鹿，以边缘参差、形似葡萄叶的深色斑块为特征。雄性身高近6米，是现存最高的动物，用长达45厘米的舌头啃食多刺的金合欢。与几乎所有哺乳动物一样，它只有七节颈椎，每节长达25厘米。

entries.k: The great southern supercontinent: South America, Africa, Antarctica, India and Australia.
entries.v: 南方的大型超大陆：南美洲、非洲、南极洲、印度和澳大利亚。

entries.k: The heart muscle gets a blood supply of its own, so it can work harder.
entries.v: 心肌拥有独立的血液供应，因而能更卖力地工作。

entries.k: The hormone behind brooding and milk.
entries.v: 主导孵育与泌乳的激素。

entries.k: The hormone of pair bonds and mother–young attachment.
entries.v: 维系配偶关系与母幼依恋的激素。
